versions.title: Hidden files, Compare Folders and SFTP / FTP servers
notes: Show Hidden Files (⇧⌘.) is now one switch for the whole app, columns included; the status bar says when hidden files are showing. Items macOS marks as hidden (Library, /usr…) follow it too, like in Finder.
Go ▸ System Folders opens places that are hidden by default: your Library, /Library, ~/.config, /usr/local, Homebrew and /private/var.
Copy Path in Quotes and Copy Path as URL join Copy Path (⌥⌘C) in the Edit menu.

Indexing a whole folder tree now skips hidden folders such as .git and .Trash, so they are not probed or thumbnailed, and clips indexed there earlier leave the library (unless they have a transcript).
New File ▸ Compare Folders…: compare two folders (the two panes, or any two you choose) and see what is only on one side, newer, or different. Filter the list and search by name.

Sync Folders in the same window: Update, Mirror or Two-way. A preview column shows what Sync would do first. Replaced and removed files go to the Trash, and ⌘Z undoes the whole sync. Online-only cloud files are never copied.

Servers in the sidebar: save SFTP, FTP and FTPS servers under Locations and browse them in a Server window. Download, upload, rename and delete with progress and Stop. Passwords are kept in your Keychain, never in a file.
SFTP asks you to confirm a server's fingerprint the first time and refuses a server whose key changed. Plain FTP warns that the password is sent unencrypted.

versions.title: Steadier with big libraries and network drives
notes: Fixed: "Could not open the media database (database is locked)" on the first launch or after an update, when several parts of the app opened the library at the same moment. Saving to the library also waits its turn instead of failing while a folder is being indexed.

Network drives and servers: opening a folder, moving the selection, the path bar, the window and tab titles, Finder tags, folder icons and the sidebar no longer wait for the server on the main thread. On a slow share the window stays responsive (on a test share answering in 50 ms, opening a folder froze the window about 1.4 s, now about 0.2 s, and moving through the files no longer stops it).
A disk ejected or a share dropped while its clips were being indexed no longer leaves them marked as unreadable: they are read again when the disk is back.
Linux style: the path bar separates folders with a dim "/" like GNOME Files, and the current folder is bold.

Path bar in every style: when the window is narrow, folders in the middle are left out (the first and the current one stay) instead of names shrinking to a few letters and the arrows between them disappearing. The Windows 11 address box no longer runs past the window's edge.

versions.title: Help menu, bug reports and safer updates
notes: Updates are now signed: Better Explora checks the update information's signature before reading it, downloads the new version itself, and opens it only when its checksum matches. Anything changed on the way is refused with a clear message.
Download… in Settings ▸ Updates now downloads the disk image into Downloads with a progress bar and opens it for you.
New Help menu: Better Explora Help, What's New, Keyboard Shortcuts, Report a Bug…, Contact Support, Check for Updates and Troubleshooting.

Help ▸ Report a Bug… is a short form that shows the whole report before anything leaves: app and macOS version, Mac model, your style and theme, and if you like the last lines of the app's log and the last crash report. Copy it, save it, open it in your email app, or copy it and open a new GitHub issue to paste it into. Nothing is uploaded.
Your home folder appears as ~ in reports, and file and folder names are replaced with [path] unless you tick Include file and folder names.
After the app quits unexpectedly, the next launch shows a small notice with Show Report, Copy, Save as File and Report…, and Don't ask again.
Settings ▸ Updates has a Privacy section that says what stays on your Mac and what goes online.

versions.title: Better Finder is now Better Explora
notes: Better Finder is now Better Explora. Same app, new name: your settings, tags, library, permissions and Pro license stay as they were.
The menus, windows, Settings and messages use the new name, and the app in Applications is called Better Explora.
Updating from the DMG: if the old "Better Finder" is still in Applications, the app offers once to move that old copy to the Trash.

versions.title: Background color for the window
notes: Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Background Color: give the file browser a tint of one colour. Pick Default (the usual look), one of 18 colours, or Custom… for any colour.
The files get a light touch of the colour; the sidebar, toolbar, path bar and status bar a little more. Light, Medium or Strong sets how much.
Light and Dark each get their own shade of the colour, so names stay easy to read.

Use as accent color (on by default): selected files, the sidebar icons, the selected filter and the active tab take the colour instead of the system accent. A colour you gave a sidebar place, or Gray / Custom in Settings ▸ Sidebar, still wins.
Works in the macOS, Windows 11 and Linux styles and with the transparent window (the glass takes the tint). Midnight keeps pure black behind the files; Increase contrast turns the tint off.
Settings, Get Info, the player and the Space viewer keep their usual colours.

versions.title: Extracting shows its progress, and never runs twice
notes: While an archive is being extracted, its icon shows a ring that fills up (with the percent on a big tile), and the status bar says "Extracting “name”… 45 %" with a progress bar and a Stop button.
The new folder appears only when extracting is done, so you never open a half-written one.

Asking again to extract an archive that is already being extracted (a second double-click, another tab or window) doesn't start it again: the archive is selected and the status bar says it is already being extracted. Extracting again after it finished still makes "name 2".
Right-click ▸ Stop Extracting, the status bar's Stop button, or quitting the app stops it and removes what was extracted so far.
Several archives at once: two are extracted at a time, the others wait their turn, each with its own ring.
A password-protected or damaged archive, or a full disk, now says so clearly (with Open with Archive Utility for a password).

versions.title: R3D clips open in DaVinci Resolve
notes: Better Finder no longer decodes or reads R3D files. They are still listed; Space shows a card with Open in DaVinci Resolve when it is on your Mac (free from Blackmagic Design), and says so when it isn't.
Settings ▸ Camera RAW now lists Blackmagic RAW and ARRIRAW only.

versions.title: R3D clips show their picture (removed in 0.393)
notes: R3D clips get thumbnails, hover scrub and play in Space, decoded by the R3D SDK inside Better Finder. Playback uses a quick 1K preview copy (an 8K clip takes a little longer than its length to get ready); Open in DaVinci Resolve for full quality.
Get Info shows the camera facts the R3D decoder reads: camera, sensor, reel, timecode and edge code, ISO, white balance, shutter, frame rate shot at, ND, lens, look.
A clip recorded over several R3D files plays as one clip from its first file. Nikon N-RAW (.NEV) files are listed as clips too.
Clips already listed are read again when you open their folder.

versions.title: Camera RAW card: open the clip in an app that shows it
notes: Space on an R3D or ARRIRAW clip shows a tidier card: the camera facts laid out like Get Info.

When DaVinci Resolve or ARRI Reference Tool is on your Mac, the card has an Open in button for it (for an ARRIRAW frame sequence, its first frame). Otherwise one line says which free apps can show the picture.

versions.title: Camera RAW clips listed before 0.386 are read again
notes: Blackmagic RAW, ARRIRAW, R3D and other camera files that Better Finder had already listed before 0.386 are read again once when you open their folder: BRAW clips get their thumbnails and hover scrub, ARRIRAW clips their size.

Space on a camera RAW clip: Blackmagic RAW plays in the viewer; R3D and ARRIRAW (MXF, .ari, .arx) show a card with the camera, exposure, white balance, shutter, lens, reel and timecode, and which decoder the picture needs. No more blank system panel or ffmpeg error.
ARRIRAW HDE frames (.arx) are now listed as clips, with their camera facts and the number of frames in their sequence.
Hovering a clip whose picture can't be decoded no longer moves the scrub line over a blank icon.

versions.title: Space plays MKV, MXF, AVI and MTS clips
notes: Space on an MKV, MXF, AVI, MTS or another clip macOS can't play now plays it in Better Finder's own viewer (Quick Look showed only an icon). A long clip starts in under a second, while its playback copy is still being made.
MP4 and MOV clips macOS plays keep Quick Look, as before.
While a clip plays during its playback copy, the seek bar shows how much of it is ready.
MTS, M2TS and AVI clips that are large or have AC-3 sound play again: their playback copy could fail since 0.387.

versions.title: Blackmagic RAW plays sooner
notes: Playing a 6K Blackmagic RAW clip is about 6 times quicker to get ready: a 10 second clip takes about 3 seconds instead of 20.
23.976 fps Blackmagic RAW clips keep their exact frame rate when played.
Get Info no longer names a Blackmagic RAW clip's LUT as its look when the LUT is turned off in the clip.

versions.title: Previews start sooner: clips that need a playback copy play at once
notes: MKV, WebM, MXF and other clips that need a playback copy start playing in under a second, while the copy is still being made. A 2 minute WebM used to wait about 7 seconds, a 10 minute one over half a minute.
When the copy is done it takes over at the next pause, at the same frame. Frame steps, trim and subtitles work as before.
Space on a long WebM plays it right away the same way.
Hover scrub on ProRes and DNxHR clips (camera clips too) is ready several times sooner and uses far less of the processor.
Hover scrub on long clips (over a minute and a half) shows its first pictures sooner.

versions.title: Camera files: ARRI, R3D and Blackmagic RAW
notes: ProRes clips from ARRI cameras (MOV and MXF) now have thumbnails and hover scrub, and play, compare and compress. Before, ffmpeg refused their pictures.
Get Info has a Camera section: camera, reel, timecode, ISO or exposure index, white balance, shutter, lens, look and more, for ARRI, R3D and Blackmagic RAW clips and any clip with a timecode track.

Blackmagic RAW (.braw) clips show their picture, hover scrub and play when Blackmagic RAW Player or DaVinci Resolve (free from Blackmagic Design) is installed on this Mac. Settings ▸ Camera RAW shows which one is used.
R3D and ARRIRAW clips show their size, frame rate and length, and say which decoder their picture needs (not included yet).

versions.title: Recent Folders and new windows skip folders that are gone
notes: Go ▸ Recent Folders drops a folder that no longer exists on your Mac. Folders on drives and network shares stay, ready for when they come back.
If New windows open is set to Other Folder and that folder is gone, new windows show Recents instead of your home folder.

versions.title: Faster: tabs switch at once, smoother grid, quicker hover
notes: Switching tabs is several times faster: a tab you go back to is shown as you left it instead of being built again (about 0.2 s of work before on a busy window, a few hundredths now).
Scrolling the Grid is smoother: each tile is lighter (the badges it rarely shows are made only when needed), so a frame takes about half the work and far fewer frames are late.

Hover scrub on a short clip (up to 20 seconds) starts almost at once: its frames are made in one go instead of twice, and the app no longer waits a moment before starting them (not in Low Power Mode, on a hot Mac or on a network drive). A clip without frames yet shows its first frame in about a quarter of a second instead of about half a second.

versions.title: Name column keeps its width
notes: List view: the Name column stays as wide as you made it, like Finder. Opening a folder in place or a long name no longer widens it; long names are shortened in the middle.
Drag the Name column's edge to change its width: it is remembered for every window, tab and pane, and after a restart. Double-click the edge to fit the longest name.

versions.title: Editing spreadsheets is free
notes: Editing CSV, TSV and Excel files in Space and saving them in place is now part of the free version, like viewing them.

versions.title: Faster: big folders open sooner, new files show at once
notes: A big folder opened for the first time shows much sooner: star ratings and labels are now read several files at a time (a folder of 20,000 files: about 7 seconds before, under 1 second now).

Big folders open faster every time: the list of files comes from the core in a leaner form and is read about three times faster (20,000 files: about 0.65 s before, about 0.4 s now). The app also keeps less memory after browsing big folders.
A file added, saved or renamed by another app shows within about a quarter of a second (it took about a second). A copy of many files still waits until it is done, then shows once.
Scrolling the grid and the list is smoother: pictures and videos waiting for their thumbnail show their type's icon without asking the disk, and thumbnails are prepared before they reach the screen.
Nothing else changes: the same views, columns, icons and thumbnails as before.

versions.title: Spreadsheets in Space: view and edit CSV and Excel files
notes: Space on a CSV, TSV or Excel file (.xlsx, .xlsm) shows it as a table: column names stay at the top, row numbers on the side, columns as wide as their words. Big files (100,000 rows and more) open at once.
Excel files show one tab per sheet under the table, dates as dates, and the formula of the selected cell on the line under the table.
Find Rows shows only the rows with the words you type.
Edit a cell: double-click it, press Return or just start typing. Return, Tab and the arrows move on, Esc drops the edit. In Excel files, start with = to type a formula.
Rows & Columns inserts and deletes rows and columns in CSV files. Excel files can get new rows and columns at the end (moving cells inside a workbook is better left to Excel or Numbers).
⌘S saves over the file, ⌘Z and ⇧⌘Z undo and redo. Closing with changes asks first.

Saving keeps the file as it was: a CSV keeps its separator, quotes, line endings and text encoding, and rows you didn't touch stay exactly the same. An Excel file keeps its styles, formulas, charts and other sheets; only the cells you changed are written, and Excel or Numbers works the formulas out again when it opens the file.
If another app changed the file since it was opened, Better Finder asks before saving. A copy of the file as it was is kept, and Rows & Columns ▸ Revert to Original puts it back.
Cells that can't be changed safely here (a formula shared with other cells, a table's header, merged cells, protected sheets, workbooks with macros) say why on the line under the table.
Viewing tables is free. Editing and saving them is part of Better Finder Pro (not locked yet).

versions.title: EPS, CorelDRAW and other vector files in Space
notes: Space shows EPS files again. macOS no longer draws PostScript, so Better Finder draws the Illustrator drawing kept inside the EPS itself: sharp at any zoom. Old Illustrator files (.ai saved without PDF) show the same way.

When the drawing may miss something (text, pictures, some Illustrator 2024 colours), Space opens on the preview picture stored in the file instead. Embedded Preview / Vector Drawing switches between the two, and the line under the picture says what is shown and what isn't drawn.
With Ghostscript installed (Homebrew: brew install ghostscript), Space draws any EPS or PostScript file exactly.
CorelDRAW files (.cdr, .cdt, Corel DESIGNER) show their stored picture and the CorelDRAW version that saved them, for old and new files.
Windows metafiles (.wmf, .emf, .wmz, .emz), compressed SVG (.svgz) and 2D CAD drawings (.dxf) show in Space. A 3D .dxf shows a view of its model.
These files get real thumbnails in the grid, and so do LibreOffice Draw and Visio files. Illustrator files with PDF content get a sharper thumbnail.
Filter chips: .svgz and metafiles are Images; EPS variants, CorelDRAW, FreeHand, LibreOffice Draw, DXF and CGM are Projects & Design; PostScript and Visio are Documents.
The bar shows the size in points, the format, the app and version that made the file, and its size on disk. Open in names the app that opens the file.

versions.title: HTML5 banners in Space
notes: Space on an HTML5 banner zip (an index.html with its CSS, scripts and pictures) plays the banner right from the zip, nothing unzipped, at its ad size. Replay starts it again; Show Files shows what's inside the zip, as before.
The bar shows the banner's size, its weight (zipped and unzipped), the number of files, whether it has a clickTag, and a note when it is over the common 150 KB limit.

Banners play offline. Clicks don't open anything: the note under the banner says where the click goes. If the banner needs files from the internet (fonts, GSAP, Google's Enabler), Load Online Content allows them for this view only.
An unzipped banner folder plays the same way with Space.
Banner zips and folders show a picture of the banner in the grid and the Gallery, taken about a second in.
A web page with an ad.size tag shows at that size in Space. Other zips keep their file tree.

versions.title: Telegram stickers, Android vector drawables and Lava in Space
notes: Space on a Telegram sticker (.tgs) plays it in the Lottie player, with its size, frame rate and length. Stickers get a thumbnail and play when you hover over them.

Android vector drawables (.xml) show as pictures. An animated one (animated-vector) plays in Space: rotation, moves, scale, shape morphs, trim paths, colours and fades, with play / pause and a position slider. Its drawable, animators and colours are found in the project's res folder; what can't be found is named under the picture.

Lava animations (a folder with a manifest.json and its images, or a .lava / .olava file) play in Space, show their first frame as the thumbnail and play on hover. A Lava folder still opens like a folder with a double-click.
Stickers, animated vector drawables and Lava are in the Motion filter.
Hover over an SVG with animation in Grid and it plays.
Double-click on a vector drawable .xml still opens it in its app; View XML in Space shows its code.

versions.title: WebM and animated pictures in Space
notes: Space on a WebM plays it in Better Finder (Quick Look can't on macOS 26). A short clip starts in about a second; a longer one shows its progress while its preview copy is made.
WebM with transparency keeps it: the clip plays over a checkerboard, and its thumbnail keeps the transparent parts too.
Animated WebP, AVIF and APNG play in Space at their own speed and loop as the file says. Still pictures still open in Quick Look.
Animated AVIF and .apng files get a thumbnail in the grid.
Hover over an animated WebP, AVIF or APNG in Grid to scrub through its frames, like a GIF.
APNG files are in the Images filter.

versions.title: Space windows fit the picture
notes: Caddis, Cavalry, Plate and Autograph in Space: Choose File and the other buttons sit under the player, on the right, next to the space kept for Caddis drawing its frames.
The facts line at the top wraps to two or three lines when the window is narrow instead of being cut short.
The Space window takes the picture's shape when a file opens (motion projects, Lottie, Rive and PDF), so there is no blank area under the player. Make it bigger and the picture grows, centred.
A wide file after a tall one gets the window's width back: it starts from the width you last gave it.

versions.title: More facts read from projects
notes: Photoshop files: Get Info and the viewer's Info show the Photoshop version that saved them, when they were created and saved, the color depth and mode, and the number of layers.
Figma files: their name in Figma and when the copy was saved.
DaVinci Resolve projects show the Resolve version that saved them; Final Cut Pro XML shows when the project was last changed.
Final Cut Pro XML no longer shows its file format version as the app that saved it.

versions.title: The same facts line in every viewer
notes: After Effects, Motion, Premiere, Final Cut, DaVinci Resolve, Filmora, VEGAS, Photoshop and Figma files in Space show their key facts on one line, in the same order as the other viewers: size, frame rate, frames, length, the app that saved it, layers or clips, file size.
An Info button next to it lists everything Get Info knows about the project, laid out the same way.
Motion Graphics Templates and Affinity documents show their facts with the same names and layout as Get Info.

versions.title: File info looks the same everywhere
notes: Get Info, Gallery, the search panel's preview and the Space cards show a file's facts the same way: labels on the left, values in one column, the same names in the same order.

Caddis, Plate, Cavalry and Autograph projects in Space look like the Lottie player: the picture fills the window, the key facts sit on one line in the top bar with Choose File, Render Preview or Install on the right, and Info shows the rest.
In Get Info and Gallery the project buttons sit above the facts.
Facts a file doesn't have are left out. A project's media count shows with how many are missing.

versions.title: Keep Audio Only in any format
notes: Remove Video (Keep Audio Only) now asks how to save the sound: M4A (AAC), MP3, WAV, AIFF, FLAC, or the original audio copied as it is.
Quality presets for each format: 96 to 320 kbps or variable bit rate for M4A and MP3, 16-bit, 24-bit or 32-bit float for WAV and AIFF, 16 or 24-bit for FLAC.
Advanced: sample rate (44.1, 48 or 96 kHz), stereo or mono, which audio track when the clip has several, FLAC compression, loudness (-14, -16 or -23 LUFS) and trimming silence at the start and end.
The sheet shows the estimated size and remembers your last choice.
Works from the right-click menu, the player's ⋯ menu and bar, Quick Actions and the Drop Zone's actions, on one clip or many at once. Stop removes the unfinished file.
Title and artist are kept where the format holds them. Nothing is ever overwritten: a new name is picked when the file exists.

versions.title: Cavalry in two clicks
notes: Space on a Cavalry scene without the player now has two buttons: Download Player opens Scene Group's page, Install sets up what you downloaded. Cavalry's licence doesn't let apps include the player, so you add it once.
Install finds the download in Downloads, Desktop or Documents (zip or unzipped folder), copies the player into Better Finder and the scene plays right away. Your download stays where it is.
After Download Player, Better Finder watches Downloads for a few minutes: Install is ready the moment the zip lands.
A file that isn't the player, or one from another website, is never installed on its own: Choose… lets you pick one.
Settings ▸ File Types ▸ Cavalry shows Ready, Not installed or Folder missing, with the same buttons and Remove.
Cavalry scenes in Space are drawn at the size they're shown, sharp on Retina screens. Open folders show Cavalry thumbnails as soon as the player is in.

versions.title: Caddis previews bigger, sharper and faster
notes: A Caddis project in Space now fills the window: tall compositions as tall as the window, wide ones as wide. Resize the window and the picture follows. The project's details are under it.
Frames are twice as sharp (960 px) and drawn about three times as fast on busy projects (strings: 30 s down to 9.5 s), with the first frame in a quarter of a second.
Better Finder runs a few Caddis engines side by side when that helps, and only one when it doesn't.
While the rest is drawn, the preview loops over the frames it has; you can scrub anywhere.
Cavalry scenes playing live are bigger too.

versions.title: No crash message for test copies
notes: "Better Finder quit unexpectedly last time" is asked only about crashes of your own Better Finder. Crashes of test copies of the app (made while building it) are no longer offered.
The Services in the right-click menu can never ask the app in a loop.

versions.title: Cloud folders and Services in the right-click menu
notes: In Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive, iCloud Drive and other cloud folders, the right-click menu has a section with the cloud app's name, icon and the items' state (Online-Only, On This Mac, Not Synced).

Make Available Offline downloads the files, and for a folder every file inside it (a big folder asks first). Make Online-Only frees the space. In iCloud Drive they are called Download Now and Remove Download, as in Finder.
Do Not Sync… and Sync Again in Dropbox folders, Open on Dropbox.com, Open on Google Drive and Copy Google Drive Link.
More Dropbox Actions in Finder… selects the items in Finder for the cloud app's own items (Transfer a copy, Copy link, Version history), which macOS lets only Finder show.

macOS Services work on the selected files and folders, as from Finder: New Terminal at Folder, Folder Actions Setup, TeamViewer and others appear in the right-click menu and in Better Finder ▸ Services. Choose them in System Settings ▸ Keyboard ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts ▸ Services.
The empty-space menu's own Terminal item is now called Open in Terminal.

versions.title: Caddis and Cavalry projects move in Space
notes: Space on a Caddis project now plays it: your own Caddis draws the main composition frame after frame, the first frames show in a moment and the rest fill in while it plays. Play / pause, a scrubber, the frame and time, and loop sit under it. Next time it plays at once.
Long compositions play every second (or third…) frame, at most 300, so they still last as long.
Without Caddis, or before signing in to it, the card keeps its picture and says why in one line.
Cavalry scenes play live in Space with the Cavalry Web Player you chose, with the same controls.
Without that player, the Cavalry card now says so, with Download Page and Choose Folder… right there (no need to look in Settings). A player folder that was moved or damaged is named too.

versions.title: Arrow keys in every viewer
notes: While Space shows a file, ↑ and ↓ go to the previous or next file in every viewer (Lottie, Rive, 3D, code, web pages, SVG, After Effects, Premiere, archives, templates, Motion cards, Affinity, PDF), as in Finder's Quick Look. In Grid and Gallery ← and → do too.
The viewer follows the selection: a file of another kind opens in the viewer it needs, or in Quick Look.

Keys the viewers use themselves stay: ← → step frames in Lottie and the After Effects and Premiere timelines, turn PDF pages and open folders in archives. A viewer's own ↑ ↓ (After Effects layers, Premiere edits, an archive's list, template rows, panning in Figma and Photoshop files) work with ⌥.
Quick Look in Columns and Gallery views now moves through those views (it moved the hidden list before).

versions.title: Drag the Drop Zone onto web pages and other apps
notes: Files dragged out of the Drop Zone now drop onto a web page's upload area in Chrome, Safari or Arc, and into Slack, Mail, Figma and other apps, also when the switch is on Move. Before, with Move on, those apps refused the drop.

With Move on, Finder still moves the files on the same disk. Web pages, other disks and most apps get a copy, and the label by the pointer says Move or Copy while you are over another app. Files stay in the Drop Zone unless they were really moved away.
Files that are only in the cloud start downloading as soon as you drag them out of Better Finder, so the app you drop them on can read them sooner.

versions.title: The search palette waits while you are in another app
notes: Switch to another app (Command-Tab, a click on its window, Mission Control) and come back: the search palette is still there exactly as you left it, with its words, tab, results, choice and preview or grid.
It closes with Escape, a click elsewhere in Better Finder, opening a result, Command-K, or when its window closes.

Closed with Escape or a click elsewhere and opened again within 5 minutes, it brings back your last words and tab, selected so typing replaces them. Up arrow in an empty field still brings back the last search.

versions.title: Preview and grid in the search palette
notes: Command-Y in the search palette shows the chosen result large on the right: its picture, a clip playing without sound, and its kind, size, length, frame, codec and date. The arrows move through the results and the preview follows. Command-Y again hides it; Escape hides it for now.

Command-G shows the results as a grid of pictures with each clip's length. The arrows move in the grid, Space opens Quick Look and Return opens the file. In the Visual tab Command-G switches its grid to a list.
Drag a result or a picture out of the palette into Premiere Pro, Resolve or Finder: it goes as the file (a copy, never moved).
The palette remembers whether preview and grid were on. Both are free.

versions.title: One top bar for every viewer
notes: The viewers that open with Space (web pages, SVG, code, PDF, Lottie, After Effects and Premiere projects, archives) share one top bar: the same height, a thin line under it, and buttons that show their frame only when you point at them.
The PDF viewer's bar is now at the top. In full screen it floats over the top of the page, below the camera notch.
Archives show their name, contents and any warning on one line.
Figma and Photoshop files keep their floating tools, now with the same buttons and menus.

versions.title: Empty folders say so
notes: An empty folder now says “This folder is empty” in every view, with a hint to drop files or press ⇧⌘N for a new folder.
When a search or a filter hides everything, the view says “No items match”.
Gallery no longer shows the details of a file from the folder you just left.
Small buttons (AI Review, Settings, Get Info, Tidy Up and others) use small text that fits them. Refresh in All Tags and Open in Preview are regular size.

versions.title: The final Free and Pro list
notes: Free for good: search by what is said, editing transcripts, Advanced Search, image sequences, GIF trimming, moving backgrounds, glass windows, your own sounds and Control Bar, Keep Audio Only and choosing a project's preview.
Some features are shared: the free version keeps a basic part (for example 3 transcribed clips a month, 1 playlist, 3 files at a time, Reframe to 9:16 and 4:5) and Pro removes the limits.
Nothing is locked yet: everything stays available until Better Finder Pro launches.

versions.title: Pro list: FPS, Aspect Ratio and Workspaces
notes: The FPS and Aspect Ratio columns join the AI column in Better Finder Pro, with sorting and grouping by them. Every other List column stays free.
Workspaces: Standard is free; Editor, Motion, Designer, Developer and the workspaces you save are part of Pro, and so is saving a new one.
Nothing is locked yet: everything stays available until Better Finder Pro launches. Your saved workspaces and column choices are always kept.

versions.title: Sharp icons in the search palette's actions
notes: The icons in the search palette's actions (Command-K on a result) keep their own shape: Open With, Quick Look's eye, Add to Drop Zone, Copy Path, Transcribe and the others were squeezed into squares.
The same for the file's picture at the top of the actions, the icons of results and suggestions, and the chips' icons.
The actions card is solid: the results behind it no longer show through, in every look.

versions.title: Pro trial reminder
notes: During the 14-day Pro trial, the Better Finder menu shows how many days are left. Choosing it opens the Pro page.
In the trial's last 3 days, the status bar shows “Pro trial · 2 days left” with Buy Pro in place of the key hints. After it ends it says “Pro trial ended” for a week. Right-click it to hide it.
Nothing pops up, and nothing shows before the last 3 days.

versions.title: 4:3 for Crop and Reframe, ratio always shown
notes: Crop and Reframe have a 4:3 shape, for photos, iPad screens and classic TV.
The frame's ratio is always shown next to its size while you crop, and changes as you drag the frame or type a size: the shape's name (16:9, 4:3), or the exact ratio such as 2.70:1 with Free.
A free frame that comes close to a common shape is named after it (3:2, 16:10, 9:16).

versions.title: List columns stay where you put them
notes: Dragging column titles in List view always works now. Columns no longer grow to a huge width when the window is resized or a column is turned on or off, which pushed others out of reach.
Name stays the first column, like in Finder. A column dropped before Name lands right after it.
Only the widths you set by dragging a column edge are remembered. Very wide columns saved by older versions go back to their normal width.

versions.title: Get Info in tidy columns
notes: Get Info lines up: the names on the left start on the same line as the group titles and the notes, and every value starts on one column, in every group.
Each name sits level with its value, also next to the tag fields, the stars and the Label menu.
Sizes, dates and durations use even-width digits, so they line up from row to row.

versions.title: Page sizes in one place
notes: The page's size is set from one button on the left of the bar, and the button says the size in use: Responsive · 742, 1200 × 900, Tablet 768 or Page Size.

It opens a panel with the ready-made sizes, a Custom width × height (Return or Use applies it, Up and Down change it by 1, with Shift by 10, and a button swaps width and height), and the custom sizes you used lately.
The separate width field at the right of the bar is gone. The zoom percentage stays next to the zoom buttons.

versions.title: More looks for the code card, and typed page widths
notes: The code card has many more backgrounds: gradients, soft mesh gradients, solid colours, a picture of your own, transparent and none. Pick them from the swatch button next to the theme menu.
The window button sets the card's style: macOS, Windows, a plain title bar or none, with the title, the language badge, the shadow, the corner radius and the padding around it.
New themes: Dracula, One Dark, Monokai, Nord and Solarized Light.
Copy Image and Save PNG use the same background and window style. Your choices are kept.

In Split, type the page's width in the bar (or width × height) and press Return. A width bigger than its side is scaled to fit. Up and Down change it by 1, with Shift by 10, and Esc goes back to Fit Pane.

versions.title: Responsive web pages in Split, and Swap Sides
notes: In Split, a web page now lays out at the width of its side of the window, like a browser window: readable at 100%, scrolling down inside its side, with no strips around it. Drag the divider and the layout follows, media queries included.

The size menu offers Fit Pane (responsive), the default in Split, Page Size (the page's own size, as before), and Desktop 1440, Laptop 1280, Tablet 768 and Mobile 390, scaled down to fit when wider than their side. The bar shows the width in use, for example Responsive · 742 px.

Swap Sides puts the page on the left and the code on the right, and back (the button next to Page | Split | Code, View > Swap Code and Page, or Option-Command-X). When the two are stacked, it puts the code on top. Your choice is kept with the divider position.
Page mode keeps its own size choice, Page Size by default.

versions.title: Edit web pages and SVGs beside their preview
notes: Space on a web page or SVG now opens Split: the code on the left, the page or picture on the right. Page, Split and Code at the top switch between them, and your choice is kept. Drag the line between them to share the window differently.
The code can be edited. The page follows your changes a moment after you stop typing, keeping its zoom and scroll.
Nothing is saved until you press Command-S or Save. The title says Edited while there are changes, Command-Z and Shift-Command-Z undo and redo, and closing asks whether to save.

Saving keeps the file's permissions, tags and line ends, and asks first if another app changed the file meanwhile. Read-only, locked and cloud-only files open read only, with the reason at the bottom.
Option-click something in the page to select its code.
Grid thumbnails show the saved version.

versions.title: SVG pictures that fit, zoom and play
notes: Space on an SVG shows the whole picture, centred and sharp, with no scroll bars or white strips. Image and Code at the top switch to its source.
Zoom in and out, Fit and 100% in the bar, or Command-plus, Command-minus and Command-0, a pinch, or Option-scroll. When it is bigger than the window, drag or scroll to move around.
A checkerboard button shows the transparent parts.
Animated SVGs (SMIL, CSS or JavaScript) keep playing, with pause, play and restart. The Gallery and Get Info play them too, and grid thumbnails are drawn at full sharpness.
Web pages get the same zoom controls.
SVGs run like web pages: on their own, reading only files in their folder, offline unless you allow it.

versions.title: Switching between 1, 2, 3 and 4 panes is quicker
notes: The Panes buttons in the status bar switch about three times faster, and stay fast however often you click them.
Panes you close with them come back as they were (same folder, view and scroll) when you add panes again within 30 seconds, instead of being built and listed again.
The panes you keep no longer leave the window and come back on every switch, so nothing flickers or reloads in them.

versions.title: Sidebar groups open and close smoothly
notes: Clicking a sidebar group's name quickly, over and over, now opens or closes it every time. Before, quick clicks counted as double clicks and were skipped, so the group seemed to stick.
Groups slide open and shut instead of jumping, and opening a long group (like Favorites) does less work.

versions.title: Checkboxes in every Settings page
notes: Settings ▸ Search, Updates, Transcribe and Visual Search use checkboxes for their on / off settings, like every other Settings page.
Click a setting's name or description to tick or untick its checkbox.
Settings ▸ Search: the drives you can index line up with the other checkboxes.

versions.title: A new Advanced tab in the search palette
notes: The Advanced tab now looks like Search and Visual: its conditions sit in groups you can fold (File, Frame, Media, Project, Also), each with a one-line summary of what is set.

Every condition is a soft chip with a menu: Look in, Name, Kind, Size, Date, Ratio, Orientation, Frame size, Rating, Tags, Made with AI, Project uses, Missing media, Folders, Hidden files and Only duplicates. Groups with something set open by themselves, and folded groups stay folded.

The results appear live under the groups, as rows like Search's, with size and day. Command-Return shows them in the window, Command-S saves a Smart Folder, and Delete in the empty field takes away the last condition you set.
Ask AI sits at the top: type what you want and press Return to turn it into conditions (Pro, as before).

Fixed: the name index could drop most of its names when macOS had not yet given Better Finder access to a folder (after an update), and then show a small count as up to date. Folders it can't read now keep their names. If Settings > Search shows a very small count, press Rebuild once.
Settings > Search: the Advanced row now describes the palette's Advanced tab.

versions.title: Small things lined up
notes: Sheets share one title size, and Rename N Items keeps its buttons at the bottom of the sheet.
Get Info: the Open and Change All… buttons fit their text, and the Made with AI note uses the full width.
Settings ▸ Search no longer shows an empty strip when no drive is known. In Settings ▸ Windows & Sidebar, Return no longer runs Sync Now.
Toolbar and other tooltips start with the button's name and its keys, like the rest of the app.
Spelling is the same everywhere: color, gray, license.

versions.title: A smaller, better aligned search palette
notes: The search palette's text is smaller: the search field, the tabs, the results and their folders, the headings and the colour swatches. Rows are a little shorter, so more results fit.
The words in the search field, its placeholder, the chips such as color: or in:, and the count on the right now line up with the icon on the left, in every tab and every look.

versions.title: Web pages play
notes: Space on an .html page shows the page itself, playing: CSS animations, keyframes, JavaScript, canvas and SVG animation. Page and Code at the top switch to its source.
Pause, play and restart the page, and choose the size it lays out at (its own size, 1920 × 1080, 1440 × 900, a phone…). It is scaled to fit the window.
The Gallery and Get Info play the page too, and grid thumbnails show the page about a second after it starts, once its entrance animations have played.

Pages run on their own: they read only files in their own folder and stay offline. When a page wanted fonts or scripts from the web, a bar offers Load Online Content for that page. Settings ▸ File Types ▸ Web Pages can allow the internet for every page you show.
A page that stops responding is stopped.

versions.title: Search by colour
notes: The Visual tab of the search palette now finds pictures and clips by colour. Click one of 12 named colours (Red to White), or Custom… to pick any colour. The results show how much of each picture is that colour, with a strip of its main colours under it.
Click two colours to find pictures that have both. The eyedropper button (Command-E) takes a colour from anywhere on screen, such as a frame in After Effects or a web page.
In the Search tab, type color:pink or color:#D9607E to keep only the files that are mostly that colour, like kind: or tag:.
Free and on this Mac: no AI model or Pro needed. Colours are read in the background when a folder opens, and once for files already in your library. Cloud-only files are never downloaded for it.

versions.title: A lighter tab row in the search palette
notes: The line under the chosen tab (Search, Visual, Advanced) is thinner and quieter.
While a search is still looking, its progress now fills that same line from the left instead of a second line drawn over it.
The Visual tab's eye icon keeps its natural shape, and the icons of the other tabs are the same soft grey as their names in every look.

versions.title: One search palette with three tabs: Search, Visual, Advanced
notes: Command-F and the toolbar's Search button now open the search palette, looking in the folder you are in (Delete takes the folder away to search everywhere). Command-K opens it everywhere, Option-Command-F on its Advanced tab.

Three tabs under the search field: Search (names, transcripts, tags), Visual (pictures and clips by what they show) and Advanced (size, date, frame, rating and more). Switch with Command-1, Command-2 and Command-3; what you typed comes along.

Type a description such as "drone shot over the beach last week 4k" and Search offers to look for it in Visual. Words like "last week" or "4K" are read as conditions: Visual turns them into chips, Advanced fills its fields with them.
Visual shows the best matches as pictures with how well they match and where in the clip. Paste a picture (Command-V) or drop one on the palette to find ones like it.
Advanced counts the matches as you change a condition. Show them in the window, save them as a Smart Folder, or ask the AI in plain words.
Type transcript: to search only what is said in your clips. The smaller source buttons (All, Names, Transcripts, Tags, Documents) now switch with Tab.

versions.title: Command-K finds files on external drives
notes: Plug in a drive and Command-K offers to index it: one click (or Return) and its files show up as you type, from now on each time it connects. Until then, Spotlight's results on the drive are shown under its name.
Ejecting a drive takes its files out of the results at once. Connecting it again reads it again, so changes made on another computer are found.

Settings > Search > Index drives when they connect adds every drive as it is plugged in. Each drive has its own Index tick, so you can leave some out. Network shares and disk images are only indexed when you tick them.
Adding or removing a drive never reads your Home folder again.

versions.title: Command-K: spoken words, conditions as chips, and Go to Folder
notes: Type said: in the Command-K palette to search only what is said in your clips: every sentence is listed under its clip with its time. Return plays the clip from that sentence, the Right arrow jumps to the next one, Command-Return opens the clip.
Narrow a search with conditions: kind:video, ext:mov,mp4, tag:Red or in:Animation followed by a space become chips before your words. Delete removes the last chip, the x removes any.
Tabs under the search field show what each source found (All, Names, Spoken, Tags, Documents). Tab or Command-1 to Command-5 switches between them.
Command-S saves the search as a Smart Folder in the sidebar.
Type a path such as ~/Doc/kh to jump to a folder: each part is matched on its own (Documents / Khach hang). Tab completes the path, Return opens it, Command-Return opens it in a new tab.
Go to Folder (Shift-Command-G) now opens the palette with ~/ already typed.

versions.title: Search Everywhere: the Command-K palette
notes: Press Command-K (Edit > Search Everywhere...) and type: files and folders from your whole Home folder show up as you type, even with letters missing ("invq4" finds invoice_Q4_final.pdf) and without accents ("khach hang" finds Khách hàng).

Names come from a small index of every file name in your Home folder (and the cloud folders in it), kept on this Mac and updated as files change. It reads only names: cloud-only files are listed without being downloaded.
Below the names, Finder tags, spoken words in your clips and text inside documents (Spotlight) appear as they are found.
Return opens, Command-Return shows every match in the window, Command-R reveals the file, Space after the arrow keys opens Quick Look, Up in the empty field brings back your last search, Esc closes.
Command-K on a result lists what you can do with it: Open With, Reveal, Copy Path, Add to Drop Zone, Import to Premiere Pro, Transcribe, Compress, Move to Trash.
A typo? The palette suggests the right spelling (Tab takes it) and offers to search inside documents, spoken words or Advanced Search instead.
Settings > Search: turn the index off, add external drives, or rebuild it. Connect to Server moved to Option-Command-K.
The search in the window's toolbar answers faster too: no more waiting after the last key, and results from This Mac appear while Spotlight is still looking.

versions.title: Collapsible sidebar groups and a Drop Zone
notes: Every sidebar group (Favorites, Locations, Tags, Playlists, Smart Folders) opens and closes with the arrow before its name. Each window remembers which groups are closed, and new windows open the same way.

Make your own groups: right-click a group's name > New Group..., then drag folders onto it. Rename, hide or delete a group from the same menu, and drag a group's name to move it up or down. Your folders are never moved.
The Drop Zone at the bottom of the sidebar collects files from anywhere (the file list, Finder, other apps). Nothing is moved when you drop them; it only keeps a reference.

Drag the stack out to a folder in the sidebar, a pane, Finder, Premiere or After Effects to copy or move the files, as the Copy | Move switch under it says. Hold Option to do the other one. Moves and copies can be undone, and moved files leave the Drop Zone.

Show List shows each held file (Space for Quick Look, x to let go of one). Right-click the stack for Copy to, Move to, Reveal Originals and Clear; the bolt button offers Compress, Transcribe, To JPG, Remove Background, Zip, AirDrop and Email.
Held files are kept when you quit. A file renamed or moved by another app is found again; one that was deleted is let go with a short note.
Hide the Drop Zone with View > Hide Drop Zone (Control-Command-B) or in Settings > Windows & Sidebar.

versions.title: Cavalry scenes get a real picture with your own Web Player
notes: Cavalry scenes (.cv) can show a real frame as their thumbnail and in their Space card. Better Finder may not include Scene Group's Cavalry Web Player, so download it yourself (free, from Scene Group), unzip it and choose its folder in Settings > File Types > Cavalry. Without it, Cavalry scenes keep their icon.

The player runs on its own, hidden, with no internet access: it can read only its own files, the scene it draws and the pictures and fonts beside that scene. A scene that takes too long is skipped after 15 seconds.

Some Cavalry features aren't in the Web Player yet (JavaScript layers, some filters), so a few pictures can differ from Cavalry. Pictures used by a scene are found when they sit beside the .cv file or in its assets folder.

versions.title: Caddis projects get a real picture
notes: Caddis projects (.caddis) show a real frame as their thumbnail, in Gallery and in Get Info, drawn by the Caddis app installed on your Mac (in the background, no window; a fraction of a second per file, then kept). Without Caddis, or before you sign in to it, they keep the Caddis icon.

Space on a Cavalry, Caddis, Autograph or Plate project opens its card instead of a blank Quick Look icon: the picture it has (Autograph's viewer, Plate's first frame, the Caddis frame) above the composition, size, frame rate, length, footage (missing ones in red), fonts, author and licence. Space or Esc closes it. A project with a preview video still plays it in Quick Look.
Cavalry projects have no picture yet: Cavalry keeps none in the file, and its web player may not be shipped with other apps.

versions.title: Autograph and Cavalry files are back in the Motion filter
notes: Autograph (.agp, .agt), Cavalry (.cv) and Plate files show up in the Motion filter again when you changed the Motion group in Settings > File Types with an older version. File types that Better Finder adds to a group later now join your edited group too; the ones you removed stay out.

versions.title: Viewers can no longer run code from a file
notes: A crafted Lottie, 3D, Figma, Photoshop, project or template file can no longer run its own script in the viewer: every viewer page now carries a content security policy (no eval, no scripts or connections outside the app), and Lottie animations play with lottie-web's light build, which has no expressions. Animations, thumbnails and folder backgrounds look the same.
A viewer page can read only the file it shows (and its folder) while it shows it: not the files of folders previewed earlier in the session, not through a symlink or "..".

A project page (After Effects, Premiere Pro, Motion, Final Cut, Filmora, VEGAS, Resolve) can ask for pictures and sound only of the footage its project names or files beside the project, and only into its own preview folder.
Previewing a very large 3D model (hundreds of MB) no longer freezes the app while the file is read.

versions.title: Video thumbnails and scrub strips use the Mac's media engine
notes: Hover-scrub strips are made by reading the clip once instead of grabbing 48 frames one by one: the quick strip of a 2-minute 1080p clip takes 0.2 s instead of 0.9 s and a twentieth of the processor time; the exact strip of a 4K HEVC clip 5 s instead of 11 s.

Video thumbnails and scrub strips of HEVC (H.265) clips are decoded on the Mac's media engine (VideoToolbox): a 4K HEVC thumbnail costs 0.2 s of processor time instead of 4.3 s, so the fans stay quiet. H.264 clips keep the processor's decoder, which is quicker for them.
Reading a folder of new clips uses half the cores, so the thumbnails and the rest of the app keep theirs.
The library's database keeps more of itself in memory and finds rows to transcribe, stale rows and kinds through indexes: a 20,000-item folder lists in 127 ms instead of 167 ms.
A leaner folder listing for the apps (29% fewer bytes), ready for the Mac and Windows / Linux apps to switch to in a coming version.

versions.title: Faster, cooler, lighter on the battery
notes: Big folders open sooner: the rows show first, then the Finder tags come in; Date Added and Date Created are read only when a column, sort or group shows them.
A file changed by another app refreshes the list a little later and in one go; a Finder tag set in Finder refreshes just that row. The app's own rating sidecars no longer make the folder list again.

Hover previews are prepared for the 8 clips nearest the middle of the window (was 30), never in Low Power Mode or when the Mac is hot, and the ones for clips you scrolled past are dropped. Hovering a clip never waits behind them.
The previews kept in memory are limited by their size (256 MB, more on Macs with lots of memory), not just by their number.
Visual Search reads a folder in the background only when the Mac isn't in Low Power Mode or hot, in smaller parts on battery.
Fewer timers run for nothing: the Welcome and Visual Search pages ask about downloads only while one is going on, a hidden Smart Folder tab stops checking, columns listen to their own scrolling only.
The app starts with fewer database connections and reads its licence state from the last run first.

versions.title: Your files and notes are safer
notes: Transcripts, tags and other notes are no longer removed when a folder can't be read for a moment (a disk or network share that dropped out, a folder without permission). Only files that are really gone leave the library.
Trim, Export and Remove Audio never replace the original clip, not even when the new name differs only in capitals (CLIP.MP4 for clip.mp4) or in accents.
Copying a folder into itself or into one of its own folders is refused, like in Finder (it filled the disk with copies of copies before).
Clicking a tag with a name of your own in the sidebar no longer quits the app.
Extract Here keeps everything that came out whole when one entry of a ZIP is damaged, and says which entries it couldn't extract. Old ZIPs with accented names are read too.
Dragging files onto the Trash in the sidebar (or into the open Trash) is a real Move to Trash: Put Back knows where they came from. Pasting into the Trash is refused, like in Finder.
Rename N Items: names no longer keep a space typed before or after the text.

versions.title: Settings: Updates opens at once
notes: Settings ▸ Updates no longer keeps the app busy for a long time. What's New shows the 10 newest versions; Show Older Versions adds 20 more each time.
A version's notes are made only when you open it, so the page stays quick however many versions there are.

versions.title: Settings: one Views page
notes: Settings has a new Views group with one page for all four views, in Finder's order: Grid, List, Columns, Gallery. Each part has its on / off switch, its size and its own options.
The Columns options (column width, the connector line's shape, colour, glow and dots) are now the Columns part of that page.
Browsing keeps File Types and Search. Workspaces moved under Windows & Sidebar, and Transcribe is last in Quick Actions.
Searching Settings for Grid, List, Columns or Gallery opens the Views page at that part. Your settings stay as they were.

versions.title: Path bar folders match the style
notes: In the Windows 11 and Linux styles the address bar shows the style's folders (yellow, blue) like the files and the sidebar, not macOS's blue folders. They change with Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Style.
Folders in the path bar keep their tag colour and Customize Folder symbol, the same as in the files. Disks and apps keep their own icon.
Get Info and Advanced Search results show folders the same way.
Folders inside an archive opened with Browse Archive use the style's folder too.

versions.title: Moving backgrounds use less memory
notes: Moving folder backgrounds free their memory when you switch tabs.

A moving background that stays paused for 10 seconds (window covered or hidden, or more than 3 moving at once) lets its memory go too and keeps a still of its frame. It starts again from that point when it can move.
Folders with a GIF or video background open without a pause: the file is read in the background.

versions.title: Views in Finder's order
notes: Views are in Finder's order: Icon, List, Columns, Gallery (⌘1–4). Here Icon is called Grid: ⌘1 Grid, ⌘2 List, ⌘3 Columns, ⌘4 Gallery, in the toolbar, the View menu, the right-click menu and Settings.
The Globe view is gone. Folders, tabs and workspaces that were in Globe open in Grid.
Your folders, tabs and workspaces keep the view you chose. Keys you changed yourself in Settings ▸ Shortcuts stay on the same view.

versions.title: A Lottie player with controls
notes: Space on a Lottie animation (.json or .lottie) opens a player: play and pause (button or Return), a scrubber with the frame and time, step a frame with ← and → (Shift for 10), Home and End, speed from 0.25× to 4×, and loop on or off.
See the animation's size, frame rate, frames, length and Lottie version. Its markers are buttons that jump to their frame.
Show it on a checkerboard, dark or light background. A .lottie with several animations lets you pick one.
View JSON shows the animation's data on the code card, and Play Animation goes back.
Plain .json files show as code. Only real Lottie animations open in the player.
Several selected files: ⌘← and ⌘→ move from a Lottie to the next file (← and → step frames there). Your speed, loop and background are kept.

versions.title: Code files on a card
notes: Space on a code file shows it on a card with window dots, its name and language, line numbers and syntax colours, on a soft background. JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, C#, C, C++, SQL, HTML, CSS, Shell, PHP, Go, Rust, Kotlin, Swift, JSON, YAML, XML, Markdown, TOML, Lua, Ruby and After Effects scripts (.jsx).
Pick a theme (Auto follows light or dark mode), a background, the text size, line numbers and wrapping. Your choices are kept.
Copy copies the code. Copy Image and Save PNG make a picture of the card, ready to share.
Big files open at once and get their colours as you look. Minified files wrap by themselves.

JSON: minified JSON is shown formatted, and objects and arrays fold with the arrow next to the line number (Option-click folds every block at that level). Lottie animations saved as .json still open as animations.
A .jsxbin (compiled ExtendScript) says why there is no code to show. Files in UTF-16 or Latin-1 read right, and a binary file named like code says so.
Several selected code files: the arrow keys move from one to the next.
More code types count in the Code & Scripts filter: .mjs, .cjs, .tsx, .java, .cs, .c, .h, .cpp, .sql, .php, .go, .kt, .toml, .lua, .rb and others.

versions.title: Bigger template previews
notes: Motion Graphics Templates and DaVinci Resolve templates: the preview now fills the window, centred, at the movie's or picture's own shape. A template's preview movie is often wide even when the template is tall, so it used to look tiny and pushed to one side.
Zoom the preview: pinch, ⌘ scroll, + and -, 0 to fit, 1 for actual size, or the buttons on it. Drag to move around when zoomed in.
F or a double-click shows the preview alone in the whole window. Press F again to bring back the card and controls.
If the After Effects viewer runs out of memory while playing a big template, it opens the project again with a note instead of going blank.
The card and its buttons are centred under the preview.

versions.title: Project viewers in Storage
notes: Settings ▸ Storage has a new Project viewers row: the working files of the After Effects, Premiere, Photoshop, PowerPoint, Figma, template and editing-app viewers, with their size and a Clear button.
Clearing thumbnails no longer removes these files, and template projects no longer hide under Other.
The cache size limit now trims old project viewer files too, least recently used first. Projects used in a viewer in the last 3 hours are kept.

versions.title: Pick media in project viewers
notes: In the project viewers (Resolve, Filmora, Final Cut, VEGAS, Premiere), picking a clip in the media panel now shows that clip: its picture, its sound when played, and its name in the header, instead of leaving the last timeline on screen.
↑ and ↓ in the media panel step through its clips and timelines.

versions.title: Affinity viewer, livelier templates, smoother projects
notes: Space on any Affinity document (.af, .afdesign, .afphoto, .afpub, older ones too) opens its own viewer: the picture big, plus its app and version, author, colour profile, fonts, layers, linked files (found or missing), data merge fields, styles and text.
Apple Motion effects (.moef) now move on the sample card: their Ramp and Overshoot behaviours play, with the choices of their rig.
VEGAS Pro projects are drawn much closer to their render: each event's pan / crop with its keyframes, fades in and out, and titles in their font, size, colour and place.
Filmora projects open at once: media in the bundle is unpacked only when first shown, and playing a long movie decodes it in runs, so it plays smoothly.
Bigger, easier play controls in the project viewers.
Space on several files includes Affinity documents.

versions.title: Space on many files, template Play
notes: Select several files and press Space: each one opens in its own viewer (templates, After Effects and Premiere projects, Figma, Photoshop, PDF, archives…), the others in Quick Look, one after another.

A bar under the viewer shows where you are (3 / 20) with Previous, Next and a list of all the files. ← → or Page Up / Page Down move through them (⌘← ⌘→ in the After Effects and Premiere timelines and in PDFs, whose arrows step frames and pages).
Motion Graphics Templates: Play and Open in After Effects Viewer now sit right under the picture.
Play plays the template's preview movie, or, when it has none, opens it in the After Effects viewer and plays it there.
The After Effects viewer now opens a template at its own composition. Before, it could open a small precomp that looked empty, so some templates seemed not to work.
DaVinci Resolve packs (.drfx): bigger rows with a picture of each title, a clear selection, and ↑ ↓ Home End to move through them.

versions.title: VEGAS Pro projects
notes: Press Space on a VEGAS Pro project (.veg): its timeline opens in the project viewer, with each track, event, media file and title text, no VEGAS needed.
The frame at the playhead is sketched from the media found beside the project; Play plays its sound.
A render saved beside the project with its name (Intro.veg and Intro.mp4) plays with Play Render, and Choose Preview File offers it first.
VEGAS projects get a card with their version, media (found or missing), generators and title texts, and show up in Used in Projects.
The viewer says what it doesn't draw: pan / crop, track motion, effects, fades and transitions.

versions.title: Affinity documents
notes: Affinity 3 documents (.af) show their own thumbnail, and older .afdesign, .afphoto and .afpub files use the picture they keep first.
Press Space on an Affinity document: its picture, titled with the document's name, even without Affinity installed.
The card lists the app, version, author, pages, artboards and whether the document uses files outside it (Affinity 3); older documents show their picture and file details.

versions.title: DaVinci Resolve projects
notes: Press Space on a DaVinci Resolve project (.drp) or archive (.dra): its timelines and compound clips, the Media Pool folders and the timeline open in the project viewer.
The frame at the playhead is sketched from the media, found in the archive's MediaFiles folder; Play plays the sound.
Effect names on each clip are listed in its tooltip; titles and Fusion clips show as labelled boxes.
Resolve projects show their own thumbnail and a card with their timelines and media.
The viewer says what it doesn't draw: Inspector values, effects, Fusion, colour and transitions.

versions.title: Final Cut Pro projects
notes: Press Space on a Final Cut Pro XML (.fcpxml or .fcpxmld): its projects and compound clips open in the project viewer, with the primary storyline and connected clips as tracks.
The frame at the playhead is sketched from the media with each clip's position, scale, rotation and opacity; titles show their text; Play plays the sound.
Media that moved with the XML, in the Final Cut Original Media folder beside it, is found.
Press Space on a Final Cut Pro library (.fcpbundle): its events, projects and original media are listed. Export a project as XML to see its timeline.
The viewer says what it doesn't draw: effects, title looks, colour, transitions and speed ramps.

versions.title: Apple Motion projects and Final Cut Pro templates
notes: Press Space on a Motion project (.motn) or a Final Cut Pro title (.moti), transition (.motr) or effect (.moef): it opens in the project viewer, no Motion needed.

Groups show as a tree, the timeline lists each layer with its keyframes and behaviors, and the frame at the playhead is sketched: pictures and drop zones, text with its font, colour solids, rectangles, image masks.
Transitions show Transition A and Transition B as coloured cards, effects show their source clip as a card, titles play over grey.
The parameters a template publishes to Final Cut Pro's Inspector are listed beside the tree, with their values and colours.
Templates show their own large.png thumbnail, a card with size, frame rate, fonts and media, and appear in Used in Projects and Advanced Search's Templates field.
The viewer says what it doesn't draw: behaviors, filters, particles, replicators, 3D and text animation.

versions.title: DaVinci Resolve templates
notes: Press Space on a DaVinci Resolve / Fusion template (.setting or .drfx): its published controls appear as in Fusion's Inspector, with each text's default words and font, colours, sizes, positions, sliders, checkboxes and menus (read only).
A still of the title is drawn from its Text+ layers: the words, font, colour, outline and place, at the moment most of them are on screen.
A .drfx pack lists its templates by Titles, Effects, Generators and Transitions, with their icons. Click one to see it.
Templates without a picture of their own get that drawn still as their thumbnail.
Advanced Search ▸ Templates finds Resolve templates by their text, control names or fonts too.
Other apps' files named .setting still open in Quick Look.

versions.title: Filmora projects
notes: Press Space on a Filmora project (.wfpbundle or .wfp): its timelines, the media panel and a Premiere-like timeline open in the project viewer, no Filmora needed.
Compound clips open as their own timeline (double-click). Effect clips, muted and hidden tracks, speed and reversed clips are shown.
The frame at the playhead is sketched from the project's own media, with position, scale, rotation and opacity. Play plays its music and sound.
Media packed inside a .wfpbundle is copied out once for the viewer, never changed. Filmora's stock media, which the project doesn't carry, shows as a labelled box.
Filmora projects show their own thumbnail, a card with their timelines and Used Media, and appear in Used in Projects and Advanced Search's Templates field.
The viewer says what it doesn't draw: effects, masks, transitions, titles and keyframes.

versions.title: Motion Graphics Templates
notes: Motion Graphics Templates (.mogrt) show their own thumbnail in every view.
Press Space on a .mogrt: its picture and preview movie, whether it was made in After Effects or Premiere Pro, size, frame rate, duration, fonts and the Premiere version it needs.

Its editable controls appear as in Premiere's Essential Graphics panel: text with its default words and font, colours, sliders with their range, checkboxes, angles, positions, groups and media holders (read only).
Open in After Effects Viewer opens the template's own project with its footage. It is copied out once, and only the last few are kept.
Templates made in Premiere Pro open their sequence in the Premiere Pro viewer.
Advanced Search has a new Templates field: find templates by their default text, control names or fonts.

versions.title: Sound in After Effects and Premiere projects
notes: Press Space on an After Effects or Premiere Pro project and Play: you now hear its music, voice and sound effects in time with the picture.
After Effects: audio layers and footage with sound, inside precomps too, with the Audio switch, Solo, Audio Levels, layer stretch and Time Remap.
Premiere Pro: every audio track with its clips, speed, track Mute and Solo, and the clip and track Volume with its keyframes.
Dragging the playhead plays short snippets, as in After Effects and Premiere.
A speaker button and volume slider next to Play. Your choice is remembered.
Missing media stays silent. The sound stops when you close the viewer, pick another comp or sequence, or move to another file.

versions.title: Faces, grain and clipped layers in After Effects projects
notes: After Effects viewer: characters keep their eyes and mouths. Common rig expressions are now worked out, such as a slider choosing a drawing with framesToTime, effect sliders and checkboxes, and simple maths.
Grain and texture layers clipped to the shape under them (a Photoshop clipping mask, Preserve Underlying Transparency in After Effects) no longer cover the frame as rectangles.
Track mattes and masks deep inside nested comps are now applied.
The first look at a project whose footage comes from big Photoshop files is several times quicker.

versions.title: Looping comps stay on screen
notes: After Effects viewer: a precomp looped with Time Remap and loopOut() (or loopIn()) now keeps playing past its end instead of disappearing while you drag the playhead.
Time Remap is now followed for every precomp and footage layer, and loopOut / loopIn (cycle, pingpong, offset, continue) work on any property.
Dragging the playhead over comps made of big Photoshop layers is smoother.
Photoshop viewer: moving around and zooming with layers switched on or off is about three times smoother.

versions.title: Show and hide Photoshop layers
notes: In the Photoshop viewer, click the eye next to a layer or group to hide or show it. The picture is then drawn layer by layer, with blend modes, opacity, clipping masks and layer masks. Show as Saved goes back to the picture saved in the file.
Layer effects (drop shadow, stroke...) and adjustment layers aren't drawn when layers are shown one by one.
After Effects projects that use a Photoshop file's layers (a PSD imported as a composition) now show each layer's own picture instead of grey boxes, and open much faster.

versions.title: Sync spinner for Dropbox and iCloud
notes: Files that Dropbox, iCloud Drive or another cloud app is uploading or downloading show a turning ring with an arrow (up or down), like Finder: in the Sync column of List, after the name in Grid, on the thumbnail in Gallery, and now in Columns too.
It follows along by itself: the ring appears when the upload starts and gives way to nothing (synced) or the cloud when it ends.

Download Now turns the ring at once. A file the cloud app says it is downloading turns for up to 3 minutes, then shows the cloud again until it really arrives (some downloads wait in a queue for hours).
Columns also show the other sync states: in the cloud only, waiting, conflict, not synced.

versions.title: Photoshop files on a canvas
notes: Space on a Photoshop file (.psd or .psb) opens it on a canvas like Figma: every artboard side by side, drag to move around, scroll or pinch to zoom, double-click or 0 to see it all.

Artboard names sit above each artboard: click one to zoom to it. The Layers list (L) shows groups, artboards and layers; click a layer to outline it, and copy the words of a text layer with Copy Text or Command C.
The file's own small preview shows at once while the full picture is prepared (about a second for a 200 MB file); opening it again is instant.
What you see is the picture Photoshop saved with the file: hiding a layer or its effects can't be shown. A file saved without Maximize Compatibility shows its small preview and says so.

versions.title: Sturdier scanning
notes: A file that makes reading its details hang (damaged, or on a network drive that stopped answering) no longer holds up scanning: it is skipped after a minute and tried again next time.
A big animated GIF on a slow drive is no longer saved as a still picture when counting its frames takes too long.
An After Effects comp in a Premiere Pro project whose .aep has become online only in Dropbox or iCloud shows as In the cloud only instead of being downloaded.

versions.title: Snappier browsing, less memory
notes: Moving through a big folder with the arrow keys is quicker in every view (about 3x in List and Columns, 2x in Gallery, 1.6x in Grid).
Closed tabs now give their memory back: a long session with many tabs no longer keeps growing.
The free space in the status bar is read in the background, so the window no longer pauses every few seconds while you move through files.
Group By Size puts apps in their real size group (they all went to "Under 100 KB").
Columns: the total size of a selection now counts the apps in it.

versions.title: Faster Advanced Search, fewer hangs
notes: Advanced Search walks folders faster (about 40% quicker on a big local folder, and far fewer requests on a network share).
Find Duplicates lists the same sets in the same order every time, the biggest files first.
A folder holding a special file named like media (a named pipe such as "x.mov") no longer makes browsing or indexing hang.
Extracting a large .gz file no longer loads it all into memory, and a damaged one leaves no half-written file behind.
Windows and Linux: Extract Here keeps accented file names (ZIP on Windows, 7z on Linux), and Linux says which package to install when the archive tool is missing.

versions.title: Smoother Premiere Pro viewer
notes: Dragging the playhead (or holding an arrow key) in the Premiere Pro viewer no longer lags behind the mouse: the frame is drawn once per screen refresh with the latest time, lighter while you drag, then sharp again when you let go.
Play keeps the sequence's own pace instead of slowing down and skipping, and movie clips keep updating while it plays.
After Effects comps in a Premiere project are read ahead, so they don't pop in while you scrub or play.

versions.title: After Effects comps inside Premiere projects
notes: In the Premiere Pro viewer (Space on a .prproj), a clip that is an After Effects comp placed by Dynamic Link now shows the comp itself, drawn like the After Effects viewer draws it, with the clip's position, scale and opacity. The .aep file must be on this Mac.
The clip's tooltip names the comp.

versions.title: Smoother scrubbing in the After Effects viewer
notes: Dragging the playhead (or holding an arrow key) in the After Effects viewer no longer lags behind the mouse: the frame is drawn once per screen refresh with the latest time, and lighter while you drag, then sharp again when you let go.

versions.title: Effects and Master Properties in the After Effects viewer
notes: The After Effects viewer's frame now draws three common effects: Gaussian Blur (soft backgrounds look soft, not as hard shapes), Fill and Drop Shadow.
Master Properties (Essential Graphics) are followed: each copy of a precomp shows its own text, pictures and values, as in After Effects, instead of all showing the same.
Colours driven by a simple expression that reads an expression control (thisComp.layer("Controls").effect("Color 1")("Color")) are drawn with that colour. Other expressions are still not run.
A track matte with no matte layer chosen (After Effects 2023 and later) no longer hides the layer.
A layer style with its own blending mode is left out (listed with Outlines) rather than drawn in the wrong colour.

versions.title: Premiere Pro projects on Space
notes: Press Space on a Premiere Pro project (.prproj) to look inside it without Premiere: its sequences (with nesting) or its bins as in the Project panel, with a filter, and the selected sequence's settings: frame size, frame rate, pixel aspect, audio rate and duration.

The timeline shows video tracks above audio tracks like Premiere: clips placed by their in and out times with their names and label colours, speed changes, effects (fx), transitions, sequence and clip markers, muted and locked tracks. Point at a clip for its details: source file, in point, speed, Motion, effects.

Drag in the time ruler or the tracks to scrub; the frame above shows the picture at the playhead, made from each clip's own file with its Motion values (position, scale, rotation, anchor, crop) and opacity. The playhead starts where Premiere left it. Arrow keys step a frame, Up and Down jump to the previous or next edit, L plays, K stops.
Double-click a nested sequence to open it; the path at the top takes you back. Missing media is marked Offline in red; files that are only in the cloud are never downloaded.
It is a sketch read from the project file: effects, transitions, titles and graphics, After Effects comps by Dynamic Link and blend modes are not drawn (titles and comps show as labelled boxes).

versions.title: Layer styles in the After Effects viewer
notes: The After Effects project viewer draws layer styles: Stroke (outside, inside or centre), Drop Shadow, Outer Glow and Color Overlay, so outlined titles look as they do in After Effects. Other styles (Bevel, Inner Glow, Gradient Overlay…) are listed on the layer's outline as not drawn.
A soloed sound layer no longer hides the pictures: like After Effects, Solo leaves out only the other layers of the same kind.
Projects you opened before are read again once, to pick up the styles.

versions.title: After Effects frames without After Effects
notes: The After Effects project viewer now draws the composition at the time you scrub to: solids, footage (pictures, image sequences and the right frame of movies), precomps, shape layers, text, masks, alpha track mattes and blending modes, with keyframes eased like After Effects and parenting.
Drag to pan, scroll with Command or Control to zoom, double-click or Fit to fit. Click in the frame to select a layer in the timeline. Play runs the sketch through the work area.
Outlines shows every layer's box and name; layers with effects, expressions, 3D or other things the sketch can't show get a dashed outline that says so.

It is a sketch read from the project file: effects, expressions, 3D cameras and lights, luma mattes (drawn as alpha), shape operators such as Repeater and Trim Paths, and text animators are not drawn. Render Preview shows the real frame.

versions.title: After Effects projects on Space
notes: Press Space on an After Effects project (.aep or .aet) to look inside it without After Effects: every composition in a tree (by nesting or by folders, with a filter), and the selected one's timeline like AE's: layer bars in their label colours, switches, blending modes, track mattes, parents, effects, markers, keyframes and expressions.
