Drag in the time ruler to scrub. Arrow keys step a frame (Shift: 10), J and K jump to the previous or next keyframe, Home and End go to the start and end, Command or Control with the scroll wheel zooms the time.
Double-click a precomp layer to open it; the path at the top takes you back. Expand a layer to see its animated properties, expressions and effects.
Missing footage is marked in red. A project with a rendered preview has a Play Preview button.
Everything is read from the project file: the frame area shows the composition's size and background only, and label colours are After Effects' defaults.

versions.title: App sizes in Recents
notes: Apps in Recents and in search results show their size again instead of staying at Calculating.
Opening Recents or a search stops the folder sizes still being added up for the folder you left, so the list's own sizes come sooner.
A folder size stopped by another pane or tab is worked out again instead of waiting until you scroll.

versions.title: Number keys switch tabs
notes: Click a tab bar, then press 1 to 9 for the 1st to 9th tab of that pane and 0 for the 10th, counted from the left. Works when the pane has two tabs or more.
A click anywhere else, any other key, or leaving the window ends it, so typing in the file list works as before.
Turn it off in Settings ▸ Windows & Tabs ▸ Number keys.

versions.title: PowerPoint slides one at a time
notes: Space on a PowerPoint file (.pptx, .ppsx, .potx) opens its slides in the same viewer as PDFs: one slide at a time, ← and → to go through them, type a slide number, zoom, and Full Screen (F) to present. No PowerPoint or Keynote needed.
The first slide shows at once and the others follow in a few seconds. The next time the file opens at once.
Pictures, text, shapes, backgrounds and tables are drawn; charts and SmartArt show as a labelled box. Fonts the file names but this Mac lacks are replaced by similar ones.
The bar's Open button opens the file in its own app (Keynote or PowerPoint) to edit or play it. Double-click still opens it there too.

versions.title: PDF viewer: go to a page, zoom buttons, full screen
notes: Type a page number: click "3 / 22" in the PDF viewer (or press ⌘L), type 15 and press Return. Esc leaves the field without closing the viewer.
Zoom buttons in the bar: − and +, and the zoom in % between them: click it to switch between fitted to the window and actual size (100%).

Full screen for presenting: the Full Screen button, F or ⌃⌘F. The page fills the screen on black, the bar and the pointer hide after 2 seconds and come back when you move the mouse. A click, Space, → or ↓ go to the next page, ← or ↑ back. Esc leaves full screen; a second Esc closes the viewer. Your other displays stay as they are.

versions.title: PDFs one page at a time
notes: Space on a PDF opens it in Better Finder's own viewer: one page at a time, fitted to the window on a dark background, instead of one long scroll of every page.
← and → (or Page Up, Page Down, Home, End) turn the pages; ↑ and ↓ still go to the file before or after. Space or Esc closes. Pinch, ⌘+ and ⌘- zoom; a double-click fits the page again.
The bar below shows the page number (3 / 22), previous and next buttons, page thumbnails to jump to a page, and Open in Preview. The page you were on is kept until you quit.
Double-click on a PDF opens it here too. Settings ▸ File Types ▸ PDF: untick it to open PDFs in Preview again. Open With ▸ Preview still works.
Illustrator files saved with PDF content open in the same viewer on Space, a PDF inside a browsed archive too. A PDF with a password asks for it.

versions.title: Look inside archives
notes: Space on a .zip, .rar, .7z, .tar.gz (and other archives) lists what's inside without extracting it: folders open and close, with sizes, dates, the number of files and the unpacked size. Filter by name at the top.

Right-click an archive ▸ Browse Archive (⌥⌘↓), or Browse in its Space list, opens it like a folder in List, Grid or Columns. It is read-only: nothing inside can be renamed, moved or deleted. ⌘↑ or the path bar takes you back.
Inside an archive, Space shows a file (picture, video, PDF, text, Figma, Lottie…) by reading out just that file. Right-click ▸ Extract to Archive's Folder copies the chosen files next to the archive.
Double-click still extracts the archive, as before.

versions.title: Look inside Figma files
notes: Space on a Figma file (.fig) shows its pages without Figma: drag to move around, scroll or pinch to zoom, double-click to fit, click a frame to zoom to it. Pick a page at the top left.
Text, pictures, components, gradients, shadows and blurs are drawn as in Figma. Big files open in a few seconds and stay smooth; the file's own thumbnail shows while it loads.
Older Figma files (saved before 2023) now get thumbnails in Grid, Gallery, Get Info and the Preview column.

versions.title: New Folder with Selection on top
notes: Right-click files: New Folder with Selection is now the first item, like Finder, and shows how many items it will move. It works for a single item too.
It is no longer inside Organize ▸. Settings ▸ Right-Click Menus can hide it. ⌃⌘N still works.

versions.title: A cleaner welcome
notes: The welcome for new installs (Help ▸ Welcome to Better Finder…) has a new look: one question per page with a big picture, dots for the steps and Skip setup at the bottom left.
Pick a Workspace from five tiles (Standard, Editor, Motion, Designer, Developer). Folders, the optional downloads and Free and Pro are grouped on clear cards.

versions.title: Search in Settings
notes: Settings has a search field at the top of its sidebar. It finds options inside every page, not only page names: type "loop", "cache" or "hotkey", then click a result to jump to that option. ⌘F goes to the field, ↑↓ pick a result, Return opens it, Esc clears.

The Settings sidebar is shorter and grouped as General, Browsing, Player, Quick Actions, AI and System. Sounds is now part of Appearance, Sidebar is part of Windows & Sidebar, and Control Bar, Subtitles and Transcript are together in Player Look.

versions.title: Tooltips everywhere
notes: Every icon and slider now says what it does when you point at it: the Compare position slider, the size sliders in Settings ▸ List, Grid & Gallery and Globe, the column line sliders, and the pane buttons in Settings ▸ Workspaces.

versions.title: A welcome for new installs
notes: The first time Better Finder opens on a Mac, a short welcome helps you set it up: pick a Workspace and a style, bring Finder's sidebar over, choose whether “Show in Finder” and folders open here, download the Visual Search and Whisper models if you want them, and see what Free and Pro include.
Skip closes it at any step, and everything in it is also in Settings. If you already used Better Finder, you won't see it: Help ▸ Welcome to Better Finder… opens it any time.

versions.title: Crash reports
notes: If Better Finder quits unexpectedly, it asks at the next start whether to send a report. Send Report opens an email you can read first: the app and macOS version and where the app stopped (your home folder shown as ~), not your files. Show Report shows the file in Finder.
Help ▸ Report a Problem… opens an email with the app and macOS version filled in.
Settings ▸ Updates ▸ Offer to send crash reports turns the question off (or tick Don't ask again).

versions.title: Right-click the filter bar
notes: Right-click the filter bar (its empty space, or All Types, AI and Tidy Up) for File Types Settings…, Chip Style, Layout (one line or more lines), Chip Order… and Show Hidden Chips. A type chip keeps its own menu (Rename, Color, Hide).

versions.title: Finder's columns, a calmer sidebar, chip style controls
notes: New List columns from Finder: Date Last Opened, Version and Comments (right-click a column title to show them). Sort By has Date Last Opened too. They start hidden.
Fixed: after 0.273 the view buttons in the toolbar didn't follow ⌘1 to ⌘5 (the view changed, the toolbar stayed on List).
Standard now shows Finder's own columns: Name, Size, Kind, Tags and Date Added. Every built-in workspace opens one pane in List; set it up yourself and Save Changes if you like.
Fixed: switching to a built-in workspace moved the Sync Status column to the far right, an empty column title in Dropbox and iCloud folders. It's back after Name.
The sidebar is a calm neutral grey that matches the files and tabs in Light and Dark, instead of taking the desktop picture's tint. Settings ▸ Sidebar ▸ Background brings the translucent one back.

Settings ▸ File Types ▸ Chip style ▸ Advanced: how grey the chips are, how strong and wide their edges are, and how much colour the icons have (down to plain grey). The preview follows as you move them; Reset puts them back.

versions.title: Workspaces, a calmer filter bar
notes: Workspaces: the new Workspace button in the toolbar (left of the view buttons) switches the List columns, the view, the panes and the sidebar in one click. Standard is a plain Finder-like list; Editor, Motion, Designer and Developer show the columns for that work, with the AI column.

Change anything after switching and the button shows a dot: Save Changes to this Workspace keeps it, Reset to Saved Layout goes back, Save as New Workspace… makes your own. Window ▸ Workspace and ⌥⌘1 to ⌥⌘9 switch too.
Settings ▸ Workspaces: drag to reorder, double-click to rename, tick the columns each workspace shows, choose its panes, view and sidebar. Folders with their own View Options keep them.

The filter bar stays on one line: the types that don't fit go into More, the one you picked always shows. All Types, AI and Tidy Up sit quietly at the right end. Settings ▸ File Types ▸ Layout brings back every chip on more lines.
The chips are calmer: a light grey pill with the type's colour on its icon, the count in grey. A colour you give a chip now shows on its icon.
Settings ▸ File Types ▸ Chip Order: drag the types into the order you want on the filter bar.
The tab bar is lighter: a softer groove and a selected tab without an outline.

versions.title: Transcribe in the background
notes: Settings ▸ Transcribe ▸ Transcribe clips in the background: the clips of each folder you open get a transcript by themselves, one at a time, so Transcript search finds what is said without transcribing by hand. Off until you switch it on.

It runs only on this Mac (never a paid cloud service), only while the Mac is plugged in, not in Low Power Mode and not hot, and never on network drives. Your own transcriptions always go first: one of yours stops the background clip at once.
A clip that already has a transcript is never transcribed again, so your own edits are kept. Clips without speech are remembered and not tried again until they change.
It uses an official Whisper model when one is downloaded (Large v3 Turbo 8-bit knows every language), otherwise macOS Speech. Settings shows what it's doing now.

versions.title: Switch off the searches you don't use
notes: Settings ▸ Search: switch off Transcripts, Visual or Advanced… if you don't use them. They're greyed out in the search panel and the search bar, nothing is read for them in the background, and the page shows how much space their models take, with a link to delete them. Names (like Finder's own search) always stays on.
Settings ▸ Transcribe suggests the 8-bit Large v3 Turbo first: as accurate as the full Turbo at half the size (874 MB instead of 1.6 GB) and half the memory. The 5-bit one (574 MB) is there too.
When an official Whisper model newer than this version's list appears on Hugging Face, Settings ▸ Transcribe offers it to download (checked at most once a day).
Cloud transcription: OpenAI's new gpt-transcribe model can be picked. Like gpt-4o-transcribe it gives no timestamps; whisper-1 stays the recommended one.

versions.title: More of Finder: Delete Immediately, Rotate, Hide Sidebar
notes: File ▸ Delete Immediately… (⌥⌘⌫) deletes the selection without the Trash, after asking. In the right-click menu, hold ⌥ and Move to Trash becomes Delete Immediately…. Locked items are asked about before anything is deleted.

Quick Actions ▸ Rotate Left and Rotate Right turn pictures in place (JPEG, HEIC, TIFF, PNG, BMP, GIF). JPEG, HEIC and TIFF are not compressed again: only their orientation changes. Edit ▸ Undo turns them back.
View ▸ Hide Sidebar / Show Sidebar (⌃⌘S). New windows open the same way.
Go menu: Recents (⇧⌘F), Computer (⇧⌘C, all your disks), AirDrop (⇧⌘R), iCloud Drive, Utilities (⇧⌘U) and Recent Folders.
Window menu: Zoom, Move Tab to New Window, Merge All Windows and Bring All to Front.
Right-click a folder of yours in the sidebar ▸ Rename. A folder in the sidebar now follows when you rename or move it.
Right-click empty space: Show View Options, and Gallery in View as.

versions.title: Visual Search download while the model updates
notes: Settings ▸ Visual Search: while the new model is downloading by itself after an update, the pane shows its progress at once, and clicking Download no longer shows an "already downloading" error.

versions.title: Crash fixes
notes: Fixed: Better Finder quit when you clicked the Search button in the toolbar or pressed ⌘F.

Fixed: Better Finder could quit when it was opened by opening a folder or file with it (Open With, a double-click, Show in Finder from another app). The folder now opens in a tab once the window is ready.
Fixed: a rare crash in Compare when the sound buttons had nothing selected.
Moving or pasting thousands of files into another folder no longer pauses the app for a moment.

versions.title: Visual Search gets a new model
notes: Visual Search and Find Similar now use Google's SigLIP model (licence Apache 2.0, about 213 MB) instead of Apple's MobileCLIP, whose licence allows research use only. In our tests it finds the right picture first a little more often than before.

If Visual Search is on, the new model downloads by itself once, in the background, and the old one (about 210 MB) is deleted. Pictures and videos are then read again as their folders open, like the first time. Until a folder has been read again, a search there finds only what has been read so far.
Settings ▸ Visual Search shows the model's maker and licence.

versions.title: Acknowledgements, and Remove Background without BRIA
notes: Better Finder ▸ About Better Finder has a new window with the version, the website and an Acknowledgements button. Help ▸ Acknowledgements opens the same list: the open-source software, data and AI models Better Finder uses, each with its licence (⌘F finds in it).

Remove Background no longer offers BRIA RMBG, because its licence allows only non-commercial use. If you had chosen it, BiRefNet General is used when you have it, otherwise Apple Vision. The BRIA model file (about 1 GB) goes to the Trash the next time Better Finder starts. Models you added yourself are not touched.

versions.title: Crop and Reframe: clearer shapes, Tab between the size boxes
notes: The shapes in Crop and Reframe come in two groups: Free (and Original in Crop) on the left, then a gap, then the fixed shapes 1:1, 4:5, 9:16, 16:9 and 21:9. It is still one choice: picking a shape in one group clears the other.
In the size boxes, Tab applies what you typed and goes from width to height, Shift-Tab from height back to width. Tab in the height box goes back to the width box. Esc still cancels.

versions.title: Crop and Reframe: type the exact size, new 21:9
notes: Crop and Reframe show the width and height of the result in two boxes under Shape. They follow the frame as you drag it, and clicking a shape shows at once what size it gives (1:1 on a 1920 × 1080 picture: 1080 × 1080).

Type a size and press Return (or Tab, or click elsewhere): the frame takes exactly that size, around its centre. With Free the other side stays as it is, so 1080 typed for the width of a 1920 × 1080 picture gives 1080 × 1080. With a shape the other side follows the shape.

A size that doesn't fit is changed to the largest (or smallest) one that does, and the box flashes red. Video sizes are even numbers. The Up and Down arrows change the size by 1 (2 for video), with Shift by 10.
What you see is what you get: Reframe now saves a smaller frame at its own size (a 720 × 1280 frame gives a 720 × 1280 video). It used to scale it up to the full height.
New shape 21:9 in Crop and Reframe, and 16:9 in Reframe (handy for vertical clips). Blurred Background works with them too; its size is shown but set by the shape.

versions.title: Smoother browsing in big folders
notes: Moving the selection with the arrow keys or the mouse is up to twice as fast in List, Grid and Columns, and about a third faster in Gallery: the path bar no longer rebuilds the folders it already shows.

Group By Date Added, Date Modified or Date Created no longer slows big folders down: a folder of 20,000 files opens in about a second instead of three, and each selection change in Grid view is instant again instead of taking more than half a second.
Scrolling the list draws rows a little quicker, and opening a big folder in Columns view does less work.
While a clip plays, the player uses less of the computer.
Nothing else changes: the same files, groups, order and look as before.

versions.title: New files show up right away
notes: A file you make in Better Finder (Crop, Convert Image, Reframe, Compress, Trim, Duplicate, paste, New Folder, Extract, Remove Background, Create PDF) is selected and scrolled into view at once, also in folders opened through a link such as ~/Dropbox. Before, with Date Added newest first it landed at the top, out of sight.
New Folder in a folder opened through a link starts with its name ready to type again.
Disks without Date Added (exFAT, FAT, network shares): a copy, a duplicate or a file moved in now counts as added when you put it there, so it sorts and groups as new (it used to keep its old date).

Windows and Linux: files that other apps add, remove or rename in the open folder show within a second, without clicking back into the window. Files made by Quick Actions are selected and scrolled into view.

versions.title: Faster folders on the Mac
notes: Opening a big folder is about a third quicker: Better Finder reads the whole folder in one go instead of asking about each file, and no longer looks at each file twice for its rating.
Going back to a folder you have opened before is quicker too: the check for new or removed files no longer looks at every picture and document again.
Nothing else changes: the same files, sizes, dates, ratings and order as before.

versions.title: Faster big folders on Windows and Linux
notes: Windows and Linux: in Columns, moving through a folder of thousands of files with the arrow keys is about ten times faster (each step no longer redraws the whole column).
Windows and Linux: scrolling Details and Large icons does less work per frame, and the player opens faster when the folder has thousands of clips.
Windows and Linux: Show in Explorer / Files no longer freezes the window while the file manager opens.
Nothing changes on the Mac.

versions.title: Crop for pictures
notes: Right-click a picture ▸ Quick Actions ▸ Crop… to cut it to the part you want, with the same frame and 8 handles as Reframe. Shapes: Free, Original (the picture's own), 1:1, 4:5, 9:16 and 16:9. The last shape you used is remembered.
Drag the frame to move it and its handles to resize it. In Free, hold Shift to keep the frame's shape. Double-click resets the frame. The new size in pixels shows under the picture as you drag.

The cropped copy goes next to the original as photo_crop.jpg (then photo_crop 2.jpg), never over a file. It keeps the format (JPEG, PNG, HEIC, TIFF, GIF), the full quality of the pixels you keep, the colour profile and the photo's details. Phone photos are cropped the way they look, upright.
WebP and Photoshop files are saved as PNG (the window says so). A GIF keeps its first frame. Undo (⌘Z) takes the copy away again.
Crop is free.

versions.title: Reframe with a free crop and handles
notes: Reframe has a fourth shape, Free: any width and height, saved at the size you crop (clip_free.mp4). Hold Shift while dragging a handle to keep the frame's shape.

The crop frame has 8 handles (corners and edges) to resize it. With 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1 the frame keeps its shape, and a smaller frame zooms in: the new file keeps the size of the full frame for that shape (9:16 from a 1920 × 1080 clip is always 606 × 1080, however far you zoom in).
The size of the new file shows under the preview while you drag. Double-click the picture to reset the frame.
Blurred Background is greyed out with Free (it needs a shape) and comes back when you pick 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1.
The Export button in the Reframe window no longer touches the window's right edge.

versions.title: Play as Queue keeps Compare's order
notes: Play as Queue from Compare always plays the clips in Compare's order (A, B, C), also when Shuffle was on: Shuffle turns off for that Queue and you can turn it back on.
Undo after Play as Queue brings back the previous Queue together with its Shuffle setting.

versions.title: From Compare to the player and back
notes: The Queue has a Compare button in its header, next to Sort, Repeat and Shuffle. It compares the whole Queue, or the clips selected in it.

Compare opened from the file list has a Play as Queue button at the left of its bottom bar. The videos you compare go to the player as its Queue, in Compare's order, starting on the one you hear (Sound off: the reference) at the same time, paused.
If that replaces a Queue, "Queue replaced · Undo" shows for a few seconds and Undo brings the old Queue back.
From that player, Compare Queue goes back to Compare and Back to Player returns, so you can switch both ways.

versions.title: Interactive Rive files respond again
notes: Rive files whose buttons did nothing in the Gallery's big preview and the viewer now respond: pose pickers, story prompts, game start buttons. The file's own state machine now starts the way Rive's editor plays it.
A Rive file's sound plays only in the Gallery's big preview and the viewer (after a click inside). Tiles you pass over and folder backgrounds stay silent.
Windows and Linux: in Large Icons, a Rive file under the pointer follows the pointer's moves (eyes that look at it), as on the Mac. A click still selects the file.

versions.title: Back to Player from Compare
notes: Compare opened from the player has a Back to Player button at the left of its bottom bar. Esc does the same (on an enlarged tile, Esc first goes back to the grid), and so does closing the Compare window: the player always stays open.
Back in the player you are on the clip that was playing when you opened Compare, at the same place, paused.
Esc on the Compare grid now also closes Compare when it was opened from the file list.

versions.title: Compare from the player
notes: In the player, ⋯ ▸ Compare Queue (also in the Queue's ⋯ menu, ⌃⌘C) opens Compare with the Queue's videos and images, in the order of the list. Select two or more rows in the Queue first to compare just those (Compare Selected Clips).
Compare shows up to 9: with more in the Queue it takes the first 9 and says so. The player pauses while Compare is open and is just as you left it when you close Compare.
In Compare (Side by Side and the grid), click a tile to hear it. The Sound buttons follow, and Off still mutes. In Wipe, a click only moves the line: choose the sound with the buttons.
The Wipe line is now a blue line with dark edges and a bigger handle, easy to see on bright and dark pictures.
Windows / Linux: Ctrl+click or Shift+click rows in the Queue to pick several clips.

versions.title: Pane dividers in blue
notes: A pane divider you point at or drag now lights up in blue (your Mac's accent colour) instead of orange, and so does the spot where a dragged tab will land.

versions.title: Camera RAW add-ons
notes: New Settings ▸ Camera RAW: Blackmagic RAW, R3D and ARRIRAW decoding comes as optional add-ons you install from a file, so Better Finder itself stays small.
With the Blackmagic RAW add-on installed, .braw clips show their size, frame rate, length and a thumbnail, and play in the player from a playback copy (picture only for now).
The add-ons themselves are not out yet: the Blackmagic RAW one comes first, R3D and ARRIRAW later. Without one, RAW clips work exactly as before.

versions.title: Render Preview for Nuke and Fusion
notes: Nuke scripts (.nk) and Fusion comps (.comp) get Render Preview, like After Effects, Blender and Cinema 4D: a short video (or a still frame) made in the background by Nuke, or by Fusion Render Node / Fusion Studio, when one is installed.

Choose which Write node (Nuke) or Saver (Fusion) to preview with Render Preview of Write Node… / Saver…. Your own Write nodes and Savers never write their files: the preview goes to Better Finder's preview folder only.
Nuke and Fusion files have a project card: Write nodes or Savers, size, frame rate, length and the version that saved them.

versions.title: Clearer pane dividers
notes: The lines between panes (2, 3 or 4 panes) are easier to see, in every appearance and style.
Point at a divider and it lights up orange along its whole length; while you drag it, it gets thicker. Double-click still shares the space equally.
Dragging a tab to the side of a pane shows where it will land in the same orange.

versions.title: Small Pro fixes
notes: In the player, the Reframe and Remove Video buttons (and Reframe in Trim and the More menu) show a small PRO badge when they need Pro, like the other Pro buttons.
A tab you left in Globe view comes back to Globe after reopening the app, even if Globe was unavailable for a while.

versions.title: Smoother drag to reorder in the Queue
notes: Dragging clips in the Queue is easier: grab a row (by its ≡ handle or anywhere on it) and the other clips slide out of the way as you move, so it drops right where you see it. No more aiming at a thin line.

versions.title: Compare joins Better Finder Pro
notes: Compare (two files or a grid of up to nine) is now part of Better Finder Pro. Nothing is locked yet: it works as before.

versions.title: Compare: hide the info on the tiles
notes: Compare has an Info button (or press I) that hides the name and specs on every tile, so only the pictures are left to compare. Each tile keeps its letter, the reference keeps its blue outline, and pointing at a tile shows its info. Compare remembers your choice.

versions.title: Render Preview items side by side
notes: In the right-click menu, Render Preview of Composition (Scene, Take) now sits right under Render Preview, before Render Still Frame.

versions.title: Better Finder Pro, prepared on the Mac
notes: The Mac app is ready for Better Finder Pro: PRO labels, an upgrade sheet and a License page in Settings. Nothing changes yet: every feature stays unlocked.

versions.title: Better Finder Pro, prepared on Windows and Linux
notes: The Windows and Linux app is ready for Better Finder Pro too. Nothing changes yet: every feature stays unlocked.

versions.title: Better Finder Pro: licence keys and trial (not switched on yet)
notes: Better Finder Pro can now check licence keys and run a 14-day trial. It is not switched on yet: every feature stays unlocked.

versions.title: Groundwork for Better Finder Pro
notes: Groundwork for Better Finder Pro. Nothing changes yet: every feature stays unlocked.

versions.title: Render Preview: Blender cameras and Cinema 4D takes
notes: Blender: a scene with several cameras offers each one when you render a preview (the scene's active camera is chosen first). Remember for this project keeps it for next time.
The Blender card shows how many cameras a scene has and which one is active.
Cinema 4D: Render Preview of Take… lists the project's takes (Cinema 4D opens it in the background the first time) and renders the one you choose.
Cinema 4D: Python tags and generators in the project are switched off while the preview renders, and the status bar says so.
Nuke and Fusion projects still get their preview with Choose Preview File.

versions.title: Tidier Settings, and choose what the right-click menu shows
notes: Settings is grouped more clearly: General, Views, Media Player, Quick Actions, AI and Maintenance.
Fewer pages: List, Grid and Gallery share one page, so do Playback and Queue, and Convert Image and Create PDF.
Show all filename extensions and Sidecar Files moved from Windows & Tabs to File Types.
Windows keyboard shortcuts is now only in Settings ▸ Shortcuts (it was also in Appearance).

New: Settings ▸ Right-Click Menus. Untick the items you never use, in the file menu, the Quick Actions submenu and the empty-space menu. Everything is shown until you change it; Show All brings them all back.
Hidden items keep their keyboard shortcuts and stay in the menu bar. The toolbar's Action (⋯) menu follows the same choices.
Your settings are kept as they were.

versions.title: Build fixes
notes: The app's built-in engine is now built for macOS 13 throughout, the oldest macOS Better Finder supports. Nothing changes in use.
Only the Content Credentials reader is built for a smaller app; searching, scanning and browsing keep full speed.

versions.title: Use your own export as a project's preview
notes: Choose Preview File… (right-click ▸ Quick Actions, or Choose File… on the project card) makes a video or picture you exported the preview of a project. You can also drop one onto the card.

It works for project, motion, 3D and design files that have no moving preview of their own: Premiere Pro, Apple Motion, DaVinci Resolve, Cavalry, Caddis, Autograph, Plate, Nuke, Fusion, Houdini, Maya, Photoshop, Figma and more, and After Effects, Blender and Cinema 4D too.
A video or picture named like the project, next to it or in a Render or Export folder, is offered first.

The file is copied, never moved or changed: a video becomes a small preview (its first 30 seconds), a picture a thumbnail. Grid hover-skim, Play Preview, Show Preview File, Delete Preview and Settings ▸ Storage work as for rendered previews, marked From file.
A chosen preview doesn't go out of date when the project is saved. Render Preview asks before replacing it, and choosing a file asks before replacing a rendered one.
Videos, GIFs, Lottie, Rive and 3D models keep previewing on their own as before; they don't get these options.

versions.title: Render Preview for Blender and Cinema 4D
notes: Blender and Cinema 4D files get a project card: Blender's scenes with their frame range, frame rate, output size and render engine, and the Blender version that saved the file. Until a preview is rendered, they show the picture saved inside the file.

Render Preview now works for .blend files when Blender is installed, and for .c4d files when Cinema 4D is installed and signed in. You get a short video (up to 10 seconds, 720 px) to skim and play, or one still frame. It renders in the background, with progress and Stop.
A Blender file with several scenes asks which one to render (Render Preview of Scene…), and can remember it, like compositions in After Effects.

Safe by design: a .blend's own scripts never run, output nodes and caches are kept away from your folders, and the project file is never changed. A model with no camera gets a temporary one for the preview.
Show Preview File, Delete Preview, Play Preview and hover-skim work as they do for After Effects. Settings ▸ Storage ▸ Project previews lists every app's previews, grouped by app.

versions.title: Choose the composition to preview
notes: Render Preview of an After Effects project with several compositions asks which one to render. Each shows its size, frame rate and length; the main one is chosen at first and marked Main.
Tick Remember for this project and the next renders, Render Again and renders of several projects use that composition without asking.
Right-click ▸ Quick Actions ▸ Render Preview of Composition… (and Composition… on the card) picks another one any time, or stops remembering it.
With several projects selected, each one renders its main composition, or the one remembered for it, without asking.
The card says which composition the preview is from. A preview of another composition replaces the old one, so each project keeps one preview.
Compositions with the same name are told apart, and names with unusual characters render too. The project itself is never changed.

versions.title: Find and manage After Effects previews
notes: Show Preview File (right-click ▸ Quick Actions, or the folder button next to the preview's size in Get Info and Gallery) shows a project's rendered video and thumbnail in their folder.
Delete Preview removes only the selected project's preview (Delete 3 Previews for three). Other projects keep theirs.
Settings ▸ Storage ▸ After Effects previews ▸ Manage… lists every project with a preview, biggest first, with its size, Show and Delete, plus Show Previews Folder and Delete All.
Previews of projects that were moved, renamed or deleted are marked Not found and can be deleted together. Projects on a drive that isn't connected are kept.
After Effects previews now have their own line in Storage: Clear Thumbnails and the cache size limit no longer remove them.

versions.title: A shorter right-click menu
notes: The right-click menu of files and folders is about a third shorter, in four groups: open and play, the file itself, rating and tags, then three submenus.
Open With ▸ now also has macOS Finder and Terminal (and Split Pane for a folder). Play Next, Add to Queue and Add to Playlist are in Queue ▸.
Compress ▸ makes a ZIP or another format. Organize ▸ has New Folder with Selection, Tidy Up by Type, Flatten and Make Alias.
Quick Actions ▸ also holds Render Preview, Check on SynthID and the transcript and thumbnail tools.
Hold Option to turn Copy into Copy Path, like Finder. Every menu bar command and shortcut is unchanged.

versions.title: Compare up to nine videos or images
notes: Compare now takes 2 to 9 videos or images: select them and right-click ▸ Compare (near the top of the menu), Quick Actions ▸ Compare, File ▸ Compare or Control-Command-C. They show in a grid: two side by side, three or four in 2 × 2, up to 3 × 3.
Every tile plays on one timeline: Play, the slider, the frame buttons, Space, ← and → move them all. Shorter clips hold their last frame.

Click a tile to make it the reference: what differs from it (codec, size, frame rate, length, file size, bit rate) is in orange on the others. Double-click a tile (or press F) to see it alone, Esc goes back to the grid. 1 to 9 pick the reference from the keyboard.
Choose whose sound you hear (A, B, C… or off). With two, Wipe and Swap still work.
A selection with folders, audio or documents in it: only the videos and images are compared, and the window says how many were left out.
With five or more clips, the ones above 1080p play from a light 540p copy (made once, then kept), so nine 4K clips play smoothly.

versions.title: After Effects previews you can skim and play
notes: Render Preview now makes a short video of an After Effects project's main comp (up to 30 seconds, 720 px) as well as its thumbnail. Hover over the project in Grid to skim it like a clip, Play Preview opens it in the player, and Quick Look plays it. You don't have to open After Effects.
Render Still Frame is still there when one picture is enough. It's much quicker.
Delete Preview removes what was rendered and the project shows its icon again. It's on the card, the right-click menu and the Gallery's Quick Actions, and works for many projects at once.
The card shows the preview's length, size and file size. When you save the project again, its preview stays but is marked out of date, with Render Again.
Rendering still runs in the background with progress and Stop, never changes the project, and works on a copy of it.

versions.title: Find pictures and videos by what they show
notes: Search ▸ Visual: type what you're looking for, like “red car at night” or “drone shot of a beach”, and the pictures and videos in this folder and its subfolders that show it come first, with a Match %.
Right-click a picture or video ▸ Find Similar lists the ones that look most like it.
Turn it on in Settings ▸ Visual Search. Download gets the model once (about 210 MB). Delete removes it again.

Everything runs on this Mac: nothing is uploaded. Each folder's pictures and a few frames of each video are read once, in the background, when the folder opens. Cloud-only files are never read, and network drives are read lightly.
English words work best.

versions.title: Premiere Pro projects, used media and where a file is used
notes: Premiere Pro projects (.prproj) get a card in Get Info, Gallery and Columns, and a tooltip: the sequences with their size, frame rate and length, the Premiere version that saved it, and the media it uses.
Used Media in After Effects and Premiere Pro cards: every file with its state (found, moved and found elsewhere, or missing in red). The arrow shows it in its folder.

Get Info of a media file has Used in Projects: the After Effects, Premiere Pro, Caddis, Cavalry and Plate projects in its folder tree that use it, with Show in Folder and Open. Projects in the cloud and not on this Mac are not read.
Advanced Search has a Projects row: Uses file (a file name or path) and Has missing media. Smart Folders keep them, and Ask AI understands "projects with missing footage".

versions.title: Reframe a video as 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1
notes: Right-click a video ▸ Reframe…, or in the player: Reframe… next to Trim (and in the ⋯ menu, or on the bar from Settings ▸ Control Bar).

Choose 9:16 (Reels, TikTok, Shorts), 4:5 (Instagram feed) or 1:1. Crop: drag the frame over the picture to choose what stays. It starts in the middle; double-click puts it back there, a click beside it brings it there.
Blurred Background: the whole picture stays, over a blurred, zoomed copy of itself (a 1920 × 1080 clip becomes 1080 × 1920).
In and Out set in the player are kept: only that part is exported.
The new file goes next to the original as clip_9x16.mp4 (clip_9x16 2.mp4 when that name is taken). Nothing is ever overwritten. ProRes stays ProRes, everything else becomes H.264.
Progress shows in the status bar and in the player, with Stop. Stopping leaves no half-made file.

versions.title: Versions of one file stack up
notes: Files that are versions of the same thing, like logo_v1.ai, logo_v2.ai and logo_v03_final.ai, or Comp v4.aep and Comp v5 approved.aep, now show as one file: the newest, with "3 versions" next to its name.

Click the arrow before it in List view (or press →) to show the older versions right under it, ← folds them again. In Icons view, click the "3 versions" badge on the picture. Right-click ▸ Show All Versions does the same.

The version is the last v12, V3, ver 2, version 4 or rev3 in the name. Words like final, approved, wip or copy after it don't make a different file; other words do (shot_010_v012_comp and shot_010_v012_plate stay apart), and so does another extension.
Group By ▸ Versions puts every file's versions in a group of their own, single files last.
Turn stacking off in View ▸ Stack Versions. Columns view and grouped lists always show every version.

versions.title: Compare two videos or images
notes: Select two videos or images and choose Compare (right-click, File ▸ Compare or Control-Command-C) to see them side by side, or one over the other with a line you drag across the picture (Wipe).
Both play on one timeline: Play, the slider and the frame buttons (or Space, ← and →, Shift for a second) move them together. The shorter clip holds its last frame.
Under each side: codec, size, frame rate, length, file size and bit rate. What differs between the two is in orange.
Formats macOS can't play (MKV, WebM…) get their playback copy as in the player. Choose whose sound you hear (A, B or off), swap the sides with X, W switches Side by Side and Wipe.

versions.title: Star ratings and colour labels that Adobe apps read
notes: Rate files from 1 to 5 stars or Reject them, and give them a Red, Yellow, Green, Blue or Purple label. They are saved the way Bridge and Lightroom save them (XMP), so Adobe apps see them, and ratings set there show here.
JPEG and PNG keep them inside the file. Other files (video, audio, camera RAW, PSD…) get a small sidecar next to them with Adobe's name: A001.mov gets A001.xmp. Videos are never rewritten.
The Rating column: click a star to set it, click it again to clear it. The Label column is in the column menu. Stars and labels show in Icons and Gallery too.

Right-click ▸ Rating and Label, or the keys: Control-1 to Control-5 for stars, Control-0 for none, Control-Delete to Reject, Control-. and Control-, to raise or lower, Control-6 to Control-9 for Red, Yellow, Green, Blue. Change them in Settings ▸ Shortcuts.
With several files selected, one change rates them all, and one Undo puts every file back the way it was.
Sort By and Group By ▸ Rating or Label, the Rating chip ("★★★ and up", Rejected, Unrated, a label), and Rating and Label rows in Advanced Search, Smart Folders and Ask AI.
Get Info has a Rating row and says where the rating is kept.
Bridge names its labels Select, Second, Approved, Review and To Do: those are read as Red to Purple and kept as they are.

versions.title: Fast on network drives
notes: Folders on a NAS or server (SMB, AFP, NFS) open several times faster: the folder is read in one go instead of asking the server about every file, and Finder tags, icons and dates no longer cost a trip to the server for each row.

Duration, frame rate and thumbnails are read for the files on screen, a few at a time, and more as you scroll. Sorting by Duration or another media column reads the whole folder, a screenful at a time. Leaving the folder stops it.

Made with AI? reads files there in large pieces (several times faster), hover previews use the quick keyframe strip, the Grid no longer prepares previews in advance there, and long audio files get no waveform there.
The status bar says Network drive. Folder sizes are still not added up on servers.

versions.title: Sidecar files go with their media
notes: Moving, renaming, copying, duplicating or trashing a video, photo or sound file takes its sidecar files along, like Lightroom and Bridge: clip.srt / .vtt / .ass, clip.xmp and clip.mov.xmp, GoPro and DJI .LRV / .LRF / .THM, .sidecar, .cos, and Premiere proxies (Proxies/clip_Proxy.mov).
Renaming gives them the new name (clip.srt becomes shot.srt). A file already there is never replaced: that sidecar stays where it was, and the status line says so.
One Undo covers the file and its sidecars; the status line and the Undo menu say "+2 sidecar files". Put Back brings back the sidecars that went to the Trash with the file.
Dragging inside Better Finder carries the sidecars; dragging to or from another app carries only what you drag.
Settings ▸ Windows & Tabs ▸ Sidecar Files: turn it off, or change the extensions.

versions.title: Sort, group and filter by Made with AI?
notes: Click the AI column, or Sort By ▸ Made with AI: Yes, Partly, Maybe, No, then files with no sign of AI.
Group By ▸ Made with AI in List, Icons, Columns and Gallery: Made with AI, Partly, Maybe, Not Made with AI, then No Sign of AI, Not Read Yet and Not Checked.
The AI chip after the file types shows only files made with AI, or only files not made with AI.
Sorting, grouping or filtering by AI reads the files not read yet in the background (up to 5,000 per folder, progress in the status bar). Files only in the cloud are never downloaded for this.
Advanced Search and Smart Folders have a Made with AI row (Yes, Partly, Maybe, No, no sign) and the AI tool's name ("Kling"). Ask AI fills them in too.

versions.title: Changing an extension asks first
notes: Renaming a file to another extension asks first, like Finder: Keep .mov or Use .mp4 (also when adding or removing one). It asks in the list, the Rename sheet and Get Info; folders and Rename N Items… don't ask.
With Show all filename extensions off, the rename box shows the name without its hidden extension and keeps it.
After a rename, Get Info shows the new Kind, icon and details right away.

versions.title: Sharing & Permissions like Finder
notes: Get Info shows permissions in a table like Finder. Click the lock to make changes.
+ adds people or groups from this Mac, − removes them. The ⋯ menu has Apply to enclosed items… (folders) and Revert changes.
The arrows of Get Info's groups no longer get a blue ring.

versions.title: Get Info in groups
notes: Get Info is laid out like Finder: Tags, General, More Info, Made with AI, Name & Extension, Comments, Open with, Preview, Sharing & Permissions. Click a group's title to fold it; the app remembers which are folded.
Rename a file from Get Info (Name & Extension), with undo like any rename.
Where from lists the page first, then the file's address, like Finder. Images show whether they have an alpha channel.

versions.title: Get Info like Finder
notes: Get Info shows Where from (the page a download came from), the size in bytes and on disk, and Last opened.
More info from macOS: camera and lens, exposure, color profile, pages, authors, sample rate, audio channels, bit rate, encoding software.
A preview of the file, the version of an app, and the original of an alias or link.
Stationery pad: tick it and Finder opens a copy of the file, like a template.

versions.title: Smaller download
notes: The app is smaller: the part that checks Content Credentials is built for size. The download is about 1.4 MB smaller and the installed app about 4 MB smaller, with the same results and speed.

versions.title: 3D models, Topaz and more AI sites
notes: 3D models (GLB, glTF, OBJ, FBX, USDZ) get the AI column too: models downloaded from Meshy, Tripo, Rodin (Hyper3D), 3D AI Studio, Hitem3D or World Labs show the site. These tools don't mark their files, so a model sent on to another Mac can't be recognised.
Videos enhanced with Topaz Video AI show it: upscaled or smoothed by AI, not generated.
Files made on Weave by Figma keep the model's own Content Credentials (for example GPT Image, verified). Weave, BFL (FLUX) and fal downloads are recognised too.

versions.title: Midjourney recognised
notes: Midjourney pictures show as Midjourney in the AI column, from what Midjourney writes into its files (its job ID with the AI source type), so they are still recognised after being copied to another Mac.
A file that only says it was made by AI takes the tool's name from the site it was downloaded from. TopView downloads are recognised too.

versions.title: Higgsfield, OpenArt and where files came from
notes: Pictures and videos made on Higgsfield are recognised (Soul, Grok, Nano Banana Pro and others show as Higgsfield). When Higgsfield ran another company's model, the AI column names it (gpt-image, Seedream, Ideogram) and the details say it was made on Higgsfield.

Files with no AI mark left in them are recognised by the site they were downloaded from, which macOS remembers: OpenArt, Higgsfield, Runway, Vidu, Hailuo, Kling, Midjourney, Sora, Luma, Pika, Ideogram, FLORA, TopView, Magnific and other AI sites. These show in grey: the weakest sign.
Details now say which site a file was downloaded from.

versions.title: Plate Thumbnails
notes: Plate projects (.plate) now show their first frame as the thumbnail, in every view and in Get Info: Better Finder draws it from the scene the way Plate does, with shapes, colours, gradients, strokes and pictures.
Effects such as blur and glow, videos and JPEG pictures inside a project aren't drawn in the thumbnail.

versions.title: Check many files on SynthID
notes: Select several pictures or videos, right-click and choose Check Files on SynthID…: the panel lists each file with its own Found, In Part and Not Found buttons, so you can drag them onto synthid.com one after another without reopening it.
Type or pick the AI tool in the panel (Google AI, OpenAI, Kling AI…) and the AI column shows it, for example Kling AI ✓. Without a name it shows SynthID ✓, or the tool the file itself names.

versions.title: Columns remembered, AI tools by name
notes: List view remembers the order and widths of its columns: drag a column title or edge, and it stays that way after quitting, in every window and tab. Reset to Default Columns (right-click a column title) puts them back.

The AI column shows the tool by name when the file says which one made it (Kling AI, Hailuo, Seedance, Google AI, Adobe Firefly, ComfyUI…). The colour tells how sure: purple is a verified signature, orange is only written in the file. Yes, Partly and Maybe are for files that don't name the tool.

versions.title: Smooth AI column
notes: Moving the pointer along the AI column is smooth now. The details open beside the column and change as you move from row to row, instead of macOS closing and reopening a tooltip under the pointer for every row.
Empty AI cells no longer show a tooltip.

versions.title: Autograph and Plate Projects
notes: Autograph projects (.agp, .agt) show the picture Autograph saves inside them as their thumbnail, in every view.
Autograph keeps the rest of the project encrypted, so Get Info can't list its comps, layers or footage: open the project in Autograph to see them.

Plate projects (.plate) get an info card in Get Info, Gallery and Columns: composition, size, aspect ratio, frame rate, duration, layers, effects and the pictures they use (missing ones in red). Hover a file in Grid or List for a summary.
Both are in the Motion group, with their app's icon.
Gallery and Columns: the project card no longer leaves some values blank.

versions.title: More AI found, clearer reasons
notes: Hailuo (MiniMax) videos and others with China's AI label are now read correctly and show the tool's name.
Pictures signed by Adobe before the current Content Credentials list (Photoshop and Firefly from 2024 and earlier) are verified again, so Generative Fill shows as Partly.
Maybe now says why: the signing certificate has expired (older Sora and FLUX files), the file is signed with a self-made certificate (Grok Imagine), or the signer isn't on the list.
WebM and MKV videos are checked too. Many are converted copies whose AI marks were removed: those stay empty.

versions.title: Kling, Seedance and China's AI labels
notes: The AI column now recognises videos made with Kling AI: Kling hides a small mark inside the video itself, which Better Finder reads. They show as Maybe · Kling AI.
Seedance videos (Dreamina, BytePlus) show the model name, for example dreamina-seedance-2-0.
Files with the AI label that Chinese AI tools must add (Kling, Jimeng, Hailuo, Vidu, Tongyi and others) show as Maybe, with the tool's name when the label gives it.
Files checked by the previous version are checked again once, so videos found empty before can fill in.

versions.title: Made with AI?
notes: A new AI column in List view says whether a picture, video or sound was made with AI: Yes, Partly, Maybe or No. Hover it to see why.

It reads what the file itself says, on this Mac: the signed Content Credentials that Gemini, ChatGPT, Adobe Firefly and others add (checked against the official C2PA list, so a fake signature doesn't count), and what ComfyUI, Stable Diffusion and similar tools write into their files. Maybe means the file says AI but it can't be proven.
An empty cell means nothing was found. That doesn't prove a person made it: AI tools that don't label their files can't be found this way.
Get Info shows the details: which tool made it, who signed it, and whether it has a SynthID watermark.
Right-click a file and choose Check on SynthID… to check it on Google's synthid.com: drag the file onto the page, then note what SynthID says. Your answer shows in the AI column with a check mark.

versions.title: No More Grey Window
notes: A blank grey window no longer appears on the desktop, mostly when quitting Better Finder. It was the hidden window that draws Lottie, Rive and 3D thumbnails: macOS sometimes moved it into view.

versions.title: After Effects, Cavalry and Caddis projects
notes: Get Info, the Gallery and the Columns preview now show what is inside an After Effects (.aep), Cavalry (.cv) or Caddis (.caddis) project: the main composition with its size, aspect ratio, frame rate and duration, the number of layers and compositions, the fonts, the app version that saved it and when.
The footage list marks missing files in red, so you see at a glance what needs relinking. Click the arrow next to a file that is there to show it in its folder.
Cavalry scenes also show their author and license.
Hold the pointer over a project in Grid or List to see the same facts in its tooltip.

Render Preview (After Effects installed): Better Finder asks After Effects for one frame from the middle of the main composition, in the background. It becomes the project's thumbnail in Grid, List and Gallery. Use the button in Get Info or the Gallery, or right-click several projects to render them one after another. Stop is in the card and in the status bar.
Nothing is rendered while you browse, only when you ask. The project itself is never changed: After Effects renders a temporary copy.
Projects without a preview show their app's icon, cleaner than before (Caddis files lost the white square around their icon).

versions.title: Saving shows its progress
notes: Saving a trim in the player now shows its progress at the bottom of the video, like Compress does in the status bar: what is being saved, the percentage and a bar. You can keep watching meanwhile.
The Stop button on that panel stops the save. Nothing is written and the original stays as it is.
The same panel shows Compress, Remove Audio, Keep Audio Only and GIFs made from the player. A quick save (a copy without re-encoding) just says Saved, with no panel flashing by.
Going on to the next clip while a save runs: the panel stays and still tells you when it's saved.
If a save fails, a message says which file and why, instead of a short note that disappears.
Stop (in the player and in the status bar) now really stops a save or a compression. Before, it could carry on and save the file anyway.

versions.title: Opens on Recents
notes: Better Finder now opens on Recents, like Finder: the files you used in the last 30 days, newest first, with Recents chosen in the sidebar. New windows (⌘N) open on Recents too.

It no longer reopens last time's windows and tabs by itself. To get them back each time, turn on Settings ▸ Windows & Tabs ▸ Reopen windows, panes and tabs from last time. If you had already picked a folder for New windows open, or turned that option on yourself, nothing changes for you.
To open a folder instead of Recents, pick it in Settings ▸ Windows & Tabs ▸ New windows open.
While Spotlight is still looking, Recents says Searching. If Spotlight is off or finds nothing, the window opens your Home folder instead of an empty list.
⌘T still opens a tab on the folder you are in (Recents when you are in Recents). Tabs showing Recents are named Recents and come back as Recents when the last session is reopened.

versions.title: Even glass
notes: Liquid Glass and Clear Glass: the glass now runs up under the toolbar, so the bar with Back / Forward and the toolbar buttons looks like the files below it instead of more see-through.
The sidebar's colour also starts at the top of the window, so the sidebar column is even from top to bottom.

versions.title: Glass Settings
notes: With Transparent window on, Settings is see-through too: the same glass and blur as the file browser, so you see the effect while you adjust it.
Settings keeps at least 60 % of its colour so its small text stays easy to read. The player still stays dark.

versions.title: See-through sidebar
notes: Transparent window: Opacity (Sidebar) now really clears the sidebar. macOS drew a light sidebar of its own under it that no setting could thin out; it is set aside while the transparent window is on and comes back when you turn it off.
With Liquid Glass or Clear Glass the sidebar gets its own glass pane, like the files. Liquid Glass stays a little frosted by nature; Clear Glass and Frosted show the most of the desktop.

versions.title: Clearer glass
notes: Transparent window: the sidebar now goes see-through too and follows Opacity (Sidebar). It turned solid before.
Liquid Glass and Clear Glass put your files on a real pane of macOS 26 glass, with rounded corners and its light at the edges.
The tabs, the address box, the column titles and the scroll bars follow Opacity (Content) instead of staying solid.
Double-click a slider's knob to put it back to its default (35 %, 50 %, 50 %).

versions.title: Transparent window
notes: New in Settings ▸ Appearance: Transparent window. The file browser lets your desktop show through, blurred like glass (Liquid Glass or Clear Glass on macOS 26, or Frosted). Off until you turn it on.
Two Opacity sliders, one for the sidebar and one for the files, tabs and status bar, plus a Blur slider. Only the backgrounds go see-through: names, icons and thumbnails stay sharp.
Tint keeps a light (Light) or dark (Dark, Midnight) veil behind your files so names stay readable over a busy desktop.
Every view follows: List, Icons, Columns, Gallery and Globe, in the macOS, Windows 11 and Linux styles. Folder backgrounds fade with the Opacity, and the window still takes every click, even at 0 %.
The player, Settings and small windows (Get Info, Advanced Search) stay solid.

versions.title: Clearer ratio shapes
notes: The shape before each aspect ratio is bigger and bolder, like on the website: in the List column, Group By titles, the Icons badge, Get Info, the Columns and Gallery info and Advanced Search. The numbers stay regular weight.
The Aspect Ratio column is now left-aligned: the shape, then the ratio right after it, and the shapes still line up down the column.

The 21:9 group is now called 2.39:1 (1:2.39 when tall), the name used for cinema scope. Same files as before: 2.35:1, 2.39:1 scope and ultrawide screens. Hover a ratio to see "Scope, also called 21:9". Smart Folders saved with 21:9 keep working.
Advanced Search: the shapes beside Landscape, Portrait and Square no longer turn white (almost invisible) after switching from Dark to Light while the window is open.

versions.title: Ratio shapes
notes: A small frame in the file's shape now sits before every aspect ratio: wide for 16:9, tall for 9:16, square for 1:1, drawn to the file's real proportions.

You see it in the Aspect Ratio column, on the group titles of Group By ▸ Aspect Ratio (List, Icons, Columns and Gallery), on the ratio badge in Icons view, in Get Info and in the Columns and Gallery info.
Advanced Search: each ratio in the menu has its shape, and so do Landscape, Portrait and Square.
The shapes follow Light, Dark, Midnight, Increase contrast and the Windows 11 / Linux styles, and turn white on a selected row.

versions.title: Aspect Ratio
notes: New Aspect Ratio column in List view (1:1, 16:9, 4:5, 9:16, 21:9…) for videos and still images. Click its title to sort from the tallest to the widest; right-click the column titles to hide it.
Group By ▸ Aspect Ratio in List, Icons, Columns and Gallery: one group per ratio, tallest first. Sort By ▸ Aspect Ratio too.
Close sizes count as the same ratio (1920 × 1088 and 1366 × 768 are 16:9), and 2.35:1 / 2.39:1 scope and ultrawide screens are one 21:9 group.
Advanced Search: pick one or more ratios and Landscape / Portrait / Square. Saved in Smart Folders, and Ask AI fills them in from your description ("vertical videos", "square posts").
Get Info, the Gallery and Columns info show the ratio, and still images now show their size (also in the Resolution column).
View Options (⌘J) in Icons view: Show aspect ratio puts a small "16:9" on each picture and video.

versions.title: Faster BiRefNet on Apple Silicon
notes: Remove Background with BiRefNet General (and Portrait, HRSOD, DIS, Massive) is about 25 % faster on Apple silicon Macs with macOS 14 or later: a newer ONNX Runtime (1.31) uses the chip's matrix units. The cut-outs are the same.

Already installed? Settings ▸ Quick Actions ▸ Remove Background ▸ Update (about 37 MB). The older engine keeps working until then; if a picture is being processed, the new one is used from the next start.
Intel Macs and macOS 13 keep the current engine.

versions.title: Rename Box Follows Its Item
notes: While you type a new name in List, Icons or Columns, the box stays on its item when the list changes: a new file sorted in above it, another sort order, folders opened or closed above it, or the window resized. What you typed and the selected part stay as they are.
If the item is deleted or renamed by another app while you type, the box closes and nothing is renamed.

versions.title: New Folder Rename Fix
notes: After New Folder, the name box stays ready to type: in List and Columns it slipped under the folder's own row a moment later (when the folder list refreshed) and looked closed.

versions.title: Remove Background Without Python
notes: Remove Background with BiRefNet and the other models now runs inside Better Finder. No Python, rembg or Terminal: Settings ▸ Quick Actions ▸ Remove Background ▸ Install downloads the engine (ONNX Runtime, about 26 MB) and the model, with a progress bar and Cancel.
Models you already downloaded for rembg are used as they are, and models you added keep working. The old rembg install is no longer needed: Settings offers to move it to the Trash.
Every model can be downloaded or moved to the Trash from the list in Settings. U²-Net and IS-Net run on the graphics chip on Apple silicon; BiRefNet runs on the processor, a few seconds per picture.
Add Model File… checks the model first and refuses files that aren't background-removal models. BiRefNet-style models can be added too.
Cut-outs keep the picture's exact colours at soft edges (no dark fringe), its colour profile and any transparency it already had. ⌘Z still removes them.
If a model is chosen but not installed yet, the menu says Remove Background (Apple Vision), so you know which one runs.

versions.title: Live Smart Folders, Drag to Reorder, Exact Trims
notes: Smart Folders keep themselves up to date while you look at them: they search again every minute (every 5 minutes for the whole Mac or several drives), a few seconds after something changes in the folder, and when you come back to the window. The selection and the scroll stay where they were.
Right-click a Smart Folder ▸ Edit Search… opens its criteria in Advanced Search; Save Smart Folder keeps the changes in it.
Drag clips up and down in a playlist (List and Icons views, in the playlist's own order) to change their order. Clips dragged in from elsewhere are added where you drop them.
Drag tags in the sidebar to put them in the order you like. Better Finder keeps this order itself (Finder's own tag order isn't changed); Use Finder's Tags brings Finder's order back.
Trim ▸ Exact frames keeps exactly the frames you see between the handles, no frame more or less.
Exporting an HDR clip (iPhone HDR, HLG, PQ) at the original quality, or burning in subtitles with it, keeps it HDR: 10-bit with its colours, and the subtitles at normal white instead of glaring.
Advanced Search ▸ Drives… searches several drives in one go, so Only duplicates finds copies of a file on different drives.

Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Affinity, Clip Studio, Sketch, XD, Figma, Krita, Procreate, CorelDRAW and Keynote / Pages / Numbers files get a thumbnail from the preview stored inside them when macOS has none (for example without the app installed).

versions.title: KTX2 Models, Rive Shapes, Stop Search
notes: glTF and GLB models whose textures are compressed with KTX2 (Basis Universal) now get thumbnails and play when you rest the pointer on them, in the Gallery and in the viewer. Before, they showed no picture.
Rive thumbnails take the shape of the animation's artboard (wide, square, tall), like Lottie, instead of a 4:3 box with empty bands.
A Rive folder background now has the artboard's shape: Fit, Fill, Size and Position in View Options (⌘J) work on the animation itself, like a Lottie or a video, not on the whole pane.

Advanced Search shows how many items it has looked at while it runs, and a Stop button (or Esc) ends a long search and keeps what it found so far. A new search, or Ask AI, stops the one still running.
When Ask AI can't answer (no key, no internet), an AI Settings button opens Settings ▸ AI.

versions.title: Open With Like Finder
notes: Right-click ▸ Open With lists the same apps as Finder, including the ones that open any file (TextEdit, Notes, Xcode, Archive Utility…). Before, a file of a type no app claims showed almost nothing.
Double-clicking a small file of an unknown type opens it in TextEdit, like Finder. Get Info ▸ Open with shows the same list.

versions.title: Linux Style
notes: A third look in Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Style: Linux (GNOME Files). Back and Forward in the toolbar with Search, the views and the menu; the folder's path as a rounded bar at the top of each pane; a flat grey sidebar; taller rows with a soft blue rounded selection; blue folders.
In the Linux style the item count floats in a small label at the bottom right of List and Grid, and the tab bar appears only with two tabs or more.
Light, Dark and Midnight work in every style. Keyboard shortcuts stay the Mac's.

versions.title: Rename in Place
notes: Rename works like Finder in List, Grid and Columns: the name turns into a box right where it is, so the folders around it stay in view. Return keeps the new name, Esc puts the old one back.

Pasting a name that was copied with a line break (from Notes, Terminal, an editor) no longer leaves the box looking empty: the line break is dropped, like Finder. Names can no longer end up with a line break in them.

versions.title: Cloud Thumbnails & Add to Dock
notes: Files that are only in Dropbox, Google Drive or iCloud show the thumbnail the cloud app keeps for them, without downloading them (like Finder).
Grid view shows the sync status after each name and Gallery shows it on the thumbnails, not only List view. A file that finishes downloading gets its full thumbnail.
Right-click a disk or a folder in the sidebar: Add to Dock (or Remove from Dock).
List view stalls less when many results arrive at once (e.g. 2,000 search results).

versions.title: Settings Sidebar
notes: The Settings sidebar is a little wider, so "Remove Background" isn't cut off.

versions.title: Fresh Media Info
notes: New clips in a folder opened in place in List view get their duration, frame rate and resolution right away (no need to go back and in again).
A clip that was still being written (a render or export landing) is read again once it's finished.

versions.title: Dropbox & iCloud Status
notes: In Dropbox, iCloud Drive, Google Drive and OneDrive folders, List view shows each item's sync status like Finder: in the cloud only, downloading, uploading, waiting or a conflict.

Files that are only in the cloud are no longer downloaded just because you browse a folder or point at them: no thumbnails, scrubbing or media info are read from them until you open them or choose Download Now.

versions.title: Disks
notes: Get Info on a disk shows its format, capacity, available space (with what macOS can free up) and used space, with a bar.
Right-clicking a disk in the sidebar: Open in New Tab, Eject, Erase Disk in Disk Utility, Get Info and Rename.
The status bar shows how much space is free on the disk you're in, like Finder.

versions.title: Media Player Settings
notes: Settings has a Media Player group: Playback, Control Bar, Queue, Transcript and Subtitles, each on its own page.
The player's ⋯ ▸ Customize Control Bar… opens the Control Bar page directly.

versions.title: App Menu Like Finder
notes: The Better Finder menu has what Finder's has: About Better Finder, Settings, Empty Trash (moved here from File), Services, Hide, Hide Others and Show All.
Check for Updates… in the same menu.
Empty Trash also works with no window open, and its confirmation always shows in front.

versions.title: Plainer Wording
notes: Messages, alerts, export choices and menus read more simply, without long dashes.

versions.title: Cleaner Settings Text
notes: Descriptions in Settings read more simply, without long dashes.

versions.title: Cleaner Tooltips
notes: Tooltips are shorter: the name with its shortcut ("Search ⌘F"), and any extra detail on a line below.

versions.title: Search Field Fix
notes: Clearing the search with ⓧ really clears it, and the cursor stays in the field to type again.
No grey hint text inside the search field any more (it showed under what you typed); the line below says what to type.

versions.title: Smoother Search
notes: Typing in the search panel is smooth again, and the hint no longer shows under what you type.
Long result lists appear a little faster in List view.

versions.title: Search Like Finder
notes: Search ▸ Names now works like Finder: it finds files and folders whose names contain all your words — anywhere on This Mac, or in the folder you're in and everything inside it.
Choose This Mac or the folder right under the search field; Save keeps a folder search in the sidebar as a Smart Folder.
Clearing the search takes you back to the folder you started from. Esc closes the search panel and keeps the results.
Folders with dots or dates in their names ("Footage 2024.10.21") are searched inside too.

versions.title: Updates
notes: Better Finder now tells you when a new version is out (at most once a day — Settings ▸ Updates). Download… opens the new version's file.

versions.title: Show in Folder
notes: Right-click ▸ Show in Folder shows a file from Recents, a tag or a search selected in its folder, right here in Better Finder.
Right-click ▸ Open in macOS Finder opens the real Finder with the file selected — even when Better Finder is your Mac's file viewer.
Showing many files from one folder opens one tab with all of them selected (Advanced Search ▸ Show in Folder, other apps' Show in Finder).
Settings ▸ Storage ▸ Show Cache Folder.

versions.title: Mini View
notes: Mini view has Previous and Next clip buttons beside Play.
Mini view can be made narrower; a long folder name in the player's title line is cut short instead of widening the window.

versions.title: Player Tidy-Up
notes: The player's ⋯ menu shows only the controls that aren't on the bar — a control is in one place, never both.
The player has no ✕ of its own any more: close it with the window's red button, Esc or ⌘W.
New default bar: Queue, Set Thumbnail, Mini Player and Full Screen on the right; Export Frame, Transcript, Cast and the edits in ⋯.

versions.title: Your Player Controls
notes: Arrange the player's buttons yourself: Settings ▸ Player ▸ Control Bar has a left, middle and right group — drag any control into a group, reorder it, or into the ⋯ menu.
New default: Repeat and Shuffle sit either side of the playback buttons, Subtitles next to the speed; Transcript is in ⋯.
Cast to Device: play the video on an Apple TV, a smart TV or speakers with AirPlay.
Trim, Compress, Remove Audio and Remove Video can be buttons on the bar too.

versions.title: Player Controls
notes: The player's controls are two rows: time played, the seek bar and the length on top across the whole width; the buttons below with Play in the middle. A narrow window no longer squeezes the seek bar.
Click either time to switch between time and frame count.

versions.title: Appearance
notes: Light, Dark or Midnight follows your Mac by default (Match the System) and is remembered only when you choose one in Settings ▸ Appearance. This update sets it back to Match the System once.
Light mode: the selected tab has a softer shadow.

versions.title: Polish
notes: Tiled folder backgrounds follow Size, Position and Rotation and always cover the whole view (smaller or bigger tiles instead of a shrunken patch).
A .lottie background keeps its own shape, so Fill and Fit work on it like on a .json Lottie.
Globe: far pictures blur without a glow around them when the folder has a background.
Too many tabs for the window: the tab bar shows the ones that fit (always the selected one), » lists them all, and scrolling over the bar slides through them.
Videos shot upright on a phone show their real size (e.g. 1080×1920) with or without ffmpeg; clips read before are read again once when you open their folder (transcripts are kept).

versions.title: Toolbar Fix
notes: The view switch's bar and pill, and the toolbar buttons' backgrounds, stay exactly behind their icons with Icon and Text on (the bar was cut off at the bottom).

versions.title: Toolbar Fix
notes: With the toolbar showing icons and text, the view switch's white pill sits on its bar again (it slid up out of it), and every button stays centred.

versions.title: Even Toolbar Icons
notes: Every toolbar button now matches the view switch: the same icon size and weight, a soft background when the pointer is over it, a raised white pill while it's pressed or its menu is open.
Group, Sort, Edit Tags and Action open their menus right under the button; Share and Edit Tags are greyed out until something is selected.

versions.title: A Softer View Switch
notes: The toolbar's view buttons (List, Grid, Columns, Gallery, Globe) are now one soft rounded bar with the current view as a raised white pill that slides when you switch — like the tabs.

versions.title: Spoken Search Fix
notes: Search with AI right after speaking (the button or Return while 🎙 is on) runs again: it waits at most a moment for your last words, then asks the AI — before, it could wait forever.

versions.title: Spoken Search Fix
notes: Speaking a search with 🎙 no longer writes the sentence twice.

versions.title: Speak Your Search in Vietnamese
notes: Advanced Search's 🎙 now listens with Better Finder's own speech recognition (macOS 26+): in the language set in Settings ▸ Transcribe ▸ macOS Speech — Vietnamese on a Vietnamese Mac — instead of the system's Dictation language, which was often English and turned Vietnamese into unrelated English.
The words appear in the box as you speak, without the Dictation pop-up; click 🎙 again or press Return when you're done. It runs on this Mac; macOS asks for the microphone once.
On older macOS the button still uses Dictation.

versions.title: Open Videos Your Way
notes: Settings ▸ Player ▸ Opening Videos and Audio: double-click (and Return, File ▸ Open, Advanced Search) can open them in the file's default app — QuickTime Player or whatever macOS uses — instead of Better Finder's player, which stays the default.
Right-click ▸ Play still plays in Better Finder's player either way.

versions.title: Advanced Search Fixes
notes: Searching the whole disk no longer lists every file twice (once through /System/Volumes/Data, where "/" really lives) — the same file was showing up as its own duplicate. A file with several hard links counts once.
Names with Vietnamese accents are found again (macOS stores them in a different form than you type), and the name search ignores accents: "buoi" finds "Buổi".
Duplicates can be found by name too: "same name — ignoring (1), copy…" lists files like "Clip.mp4" and "Clip (1).mp4" (downloaded twice, copied).
Click a column heading to sort the results (again for the other way); copies of a set stay together.
Space previews the selected results (Quick Look; Rive / Lottie in the app's viewer); double-click or Return plays clips in Better Finder's own player.
Show in Browser works when the window you searched from was closed.
Clicking Better Finder in the Dock brings a browser window back even while Advanced Search (or another window) is open.

versions.title: Clearer Cloud Transcription
notes: Settings ▸ Transcribe ▸ Show Models Folder works again (with Better Finder as the Mac's file viewer it did nothing); each model also has a Show button. Remove Background's models folder and Storage's Show in Finder were fixed the same way.
Cloud Service explains itself: what is uploaded and who bills it, what each service is good for, which model to pick, and a Get a Key button that opens the service's key page.
A status line says when everything is ready, or exactly what's still missing (key, server address, model, ffmpeg) — instead of a red error.
Custom (OpenAI-compatible) is kept while you fill in its address.

versions.title: Switch Review Views in Place
notes: Switching AI Review between Suggestions and Whole Transcript keeps your place: the line you picked stays picked and moves to the middle — in Whole Transcript with the lines around it to read.
Coming back to Suggestions from a line without a suggestion goes to the nearest suggestion.
Nothing picked: the line playing stays in view if it's on screen, otherwise the line in the middle of the view.

versions.title: Transcript Fixes
notes: Double-clicking a line's time in the transcript no longer breaks its layout (time glued to the text, wrapped lines under the time).
Clicking a line no longer leaves the previous one in bold.
The AI Review button is never cut off: in a narrow panel the language menu gets narrower, then the "Transcript" title hides.

versions.title: Tidier AI Review
notes: AI Review lines line up in columns: the tick at the far left, then the time, then the text — on every line, with or without a suggestion. Long text wraps under itself, not under the time.
The transcript beside the player wraps the same way.
↑ / ↓ next to Select None go to the previous / next line and play it; with ⇧ they jump to the previous / next AI suggestion.
Lines you pick (⇧ / ⌘-click) get a thin outline instead of a grey band, so they don't look like the line being played.

versions.title: Clearer Transcript, Review the Whole Thing
notes: The line being spoken stands out more: a stronger fill with a bar at its edge and bold text. Settings ▸ Player ▸ Transcript sets its colour, strength, the bar, bold, text size and whether it stays in the middle of the panel.
The ✨ button is now an "AI Review" button, and hovering it explains what it does (what is sent, that nothing changes until you apply, that it uses API credit).
AI Review has a Whole Transcript view: every line in order with the suggestions in place, so you can read what comes before and after.
Double-click any line there to correct it yourself; your corrections are marked "edited" and kept when the AI reviews that part again.
Pick lines and right-click ▸ AI Review These Lines to have just that part checked — also straight from the transcript, without a full review.
Right-click suggestions ▸ Remove Suggestion; Run Again keeps your own corrections.

versions.title: AI Review Beside the Video
notes: AI Review opens in the transcript panel instead of a dialog over the video: play the clip and compare the suggestions while you watch.
Click a suggestion to hear that line (playback pauses at its end); the line being played is highlighted.
Double-click a suggestion's new text to change it before applying.
Later keeps the review — the ✨ button lights up and opens it again, even after closing the player or the app, without asking the AI again. Discard throws it away; Run Again asks for a new one.
Lines changed since the review (edited, re-transcribed) drop out of it by themselves.

versions.title: Transcribe With Nothing to Install
notes: New engine: macOS Speech (macOS 26 or later) — transcribes on this Mac with macOS's own speech recognition, free and private, nothing to install. Vietnamese, English and about 50 more languages; the first time a language is used, macOS downloads it once.
